articles.title: La OCU advierte: multas de hasta 1.220 euros por circular con patinete eléctrico sin registro ni seguro
articles.standfirst: La organización de consumidores alerta de que la falta de registro y de seguro en un patinete eléctrico puede sumar sanciones elevadas, además de la inmovilización del vehículo.
articles.summary: La organización de consumidores alerta de que la falta de registro y de seguro en un patinete eléctrico puede sumar sanciones elevadas, además de la inmovilización del vehículo.
articles.body: La OCU ha lanzado un aviso serio a los propietarios de patinetes eléctricos: circular con su vehículo sin inscribir en la DGT y sin el seguro obligatorio puede costar hasta 1.220 euros. La cifra sale de sumar dos sanciones distintas: hasta 610 euros por carecer de registro y la misma cuantía por circular sin seguro. A estas multas se suma, además, la inmovilización del patinete y su posible traslado a un depósito municipal. Detrás de este aviso está el Real Decreto 52/2026, que modifica el Reglamento General de Vehículos y exige, desde enero de este año, inscribir todo Vehículo de Movilidad Personal (ese es el nombre oficial de los patinetes eléctricos) en el Registro de la DGT, llevar una etiqueta identificativa y contar con un seguro en vigor. Los modelos más antiguos, comprados antes de la norma, cuentan con un plazo que se extiende hasta enero de 2027. El registro, además, condiciona todo lo demás, ya que sin ese trámite resuelto resulta imposible contratar el seguro. Según los cálculos de la propia OCU, a fecha de abril apenas 140.000 patinetes figuraban inscritos en el registro de la DGT, una cifra minúscula frente al parque total, que supera los cuatro millones de unidades en circulación por todo el país. El susto de la multa, sin embargo, es lo de menos comparado con el riesgo que entraña de circular sin cobertura. La responsabilidad civil frente a terceros puede superar con facilidad los 200.000 euros en caso de accidente, y llegar hasta el medio millón si se producen lesiones graves, que recaería sobre el bolsillo del conductor o de sus padres o tutores, en caso de ser un menor. La prueba de que el peligro es real la respalda una estadística de la Fundación Mapfre que dice que en 2024 se registraron 396 accidentes con un patinete eléctrico implicado, con un resultado de 240 heridos y 14 personas fallecidas. Ponerse al día resulta en realidad más o menos asequible. La tasa de inscripción en el registro de la DGT cuesta 8,67 euros para los patinetes que ya vienen certificados de fábrica, a los que se suman unos 20 euros por la etiqueta identificativa homologada. Quien tenga un modelo sin esa certificación de origen deberá pasar antes por un laboratorio autorizado por la DGT, un proceso que en este caso puede complicarse y encarecerse bastante, motivo de peso para comprobar este detalle antes de comprar un patinete usado. El seguro, por que también es más caro, se mueve entre los 60 y los 160 euros al año según un estudio propio de la OCU, que recomienda ir más allá del mínimo legal, sumando cobertura para los daños propios en caso de ser el responsable del siniestro y protección frente a robo, incendio o rotura del propio aparato. La normativa añade, además, otro puñado de restricciones que conviene tener presentes. La edad mínima para circular se fija en los 15 años, sin necesidad de carné, llevar acompañante supone una multa de 100 euros, y circular por la acera o, a partir del próximo 1 de octubre, sin casco, añade otros 200 euros por cada infracción. De noche o con poca visibilidad por el clima resulta obligatorio llevar un elemento luminoso o reflectante, y desde octubre de 2027 los patinetes deberán circular con las luces encendidas de forma permanente, tanto de día como de noche.

articles.title: Arizona State's trip to London evokes memories of football in Tokyo
articles.summary: Arizona State football is playing in London on Sept. 19. Its last international trip was in 1990, and that game was quite the offensive showcase.
articles.body:
LONDON — One of the most memorable games in Arizona State football history came against Houston in 1990.

The highlight of that game, played in Tokyo, was a record-setting performance by Houston quarterback David Klingler, who threw for 716 yards and seven touchdowns. Paul Justin, the quarterback for ASU, threw for 474 yards. Houston won the game, then known as the Coca-Cola Classic, 62-45, and traditionally played in December after the regular season.

That annual showcase was played from 1977 to 1993, originally named the Mirage Bowl.

On Sept. 19, Coach Kenny Dillingham's Sun Devils (1-1) will face off against Kansas (1-1) at Wembley Stadium in London. This marks the longest road trip for ASU since that contest in which Klinger set a then-NCAA record.

Will this game, the Big 12 Conference opener for both teams, be just as memorable? Time will tell.

Arizona State football hits the road, takes on No. 9 Texas A&M

Tim Healey, the radio voice of the Sun Devils for the last 29 years, was on that trip in a different capacity. He didn't get the radio job until 1998, but he was the television play-by-play man for football and men's basketball games that aired on Channel 3.

Although that game was not televised, Healey still made the trip to Tokyo and recorded features all week for later use. He remembers it well. One thing of note: both teams flew on the same charter out of Los Angeles, something that would never happen nowadays.

"(Houston) had this run-and-shoot offense and just put up video game-like numbers," Healey said. "It was just crazy. We actually put up some really good numbers too, but we just couldn't quite keep up."

That trip to Tokyo and the current trip to London mark his only football endeavors outside the U.S.

Unlike the team, Healey actually returned to Arizona after the Texas A&M game, and flew back out on Tuesday, Sept. 15, with wife, Margie, arriving in London the next day.

He gives much of the credit for the preparation of the broadcast to producer Shawn Crespin, who is considered "essential personnel" and was on the team charter from Dallas to London.

Crespin had to weigh, label, and note the serial numbers of the equipment for documentation that comes with transporting products into a foreign country. Only the essentials were brought to London.

The team set up for the broadcast at the stadium on Friday, Sept. 18.

"The biggest thing was the conversion and making sure we were good there," Crespin said. "You connect with the venue, connect with the IT staff, and make sure you have everything you need. We've been working with them for months, so we were pretty well prepared."

This will be the first FBS game played on British soil. It is ASU's first game outside the continental United States since the 2006 Hawai'i Bowl and its second game outside the United States.

ASU also has a unique distinction in playing back-to-back road games, with one in an international setting. Arizona State is the first FBS team to play a true road game one week followed by an international game seven days later since Navy in 1996.

Healey expects the game to be right up there in his most memorable experiences.

"This is a forever thing. ASU and Kansas are playing the first game of college football in an iconic venue," he said. "American football has gotten more popular with all the NFL games being played over there. This is one of the most iconic venues in the world.

"I've gotten into Ted Lasso, and that gives you an idea of how the country views its 'football' and how passionate they are about it. Without question, it's going to be a memorable moment for the players and coaches, and all of us associated with this program."

articles.title: Oklahoma looks to continue impressive streak against New Mexico
articles.summary: Oklahoma is 2-0 against New Mexico, winning both meetings by shutout.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners will face the New Mexico Lobos on Saturday for the first time in more than 90 years. The Sooners and Lobos have faced off twice before.

The first meeting took place in 1930, with Oklahoma beating New Mexico 47-0. Oklahoma followed that up with a 25-0 win in 1935. That means the Sooners have an impressive shutout streak going against the Lobos.

However, it will not be easy to keep that streak alive, despite the Sooners having one of the best defenses in college football. New Mexico has the No. 21-ranked rushing attack at 246 yards per game. The Lobos also rank No. 7 in the country in scoring offense at 54 points per game.

The Sooners enter the game at 1-1 and are coming off their first loss of the season. The offense struggled in that game, losing to the Michigan Wolverines 17-10. They desperately need a bounce-back game.

The Lobos, meanwhile, are 2-0 with two blowout wins. The offense has put up big numbers, while the defense ranks No. 2 in the country in total defense. They pose a significant threat to the Sooners on Saturday.

Oklahoma's history against New Mexico may suggest a comfortable matchup, but the current Lobos are a completely different team. New Mexico won nine games last season and has won eight of its last nine games dating back to mid-2025. Under head coach Jason Eck, the Lobos have developed into a confident, well-coached team that has been determined on both sides of the ball this season.

That makes Saturday's game much more than a chance for Oklahoma to add another win to a decades-old series. The Sooners are coming off a loss, their offense has plenty to prove and New Mexico arrives in Norman with the production and confidence to make Oklahoma work for every possession.

The Sooners may have dominated this matchup nine decades ago, but none of that matters Saturday. If Oklahoma wants to leave Norman with a win, it will have to earn it against a New Mexico team that has every reason to believe it can pull off the upset.

articles.title: Dan’s Daily: ‘Canes Refuse Nikishin Trades? Malkin Future, Penguins Analysis
articles.summary: Evgeni Malkin may or may not be done playing hockey after this season, and he took a rather mature tone […]
articles.body:
Evgeni Malkin may or may not be done playing hockey after this season, and he took a rather mature tone on Friday. Not all of the Penguins seem happy about the glut of players, and one wonders if it's affecting camp. After a couple of days, trends and players who are on their game are emerging, including some of coach Dan Muse's early defensive pairings and potential line combinations.

Elsewhere in the Daily, it's got a Russian flavor. Alexander Nikishin 's agent shot down KHL rumors but essentially accused the Carolina Hurricanes of sitting on trades for his player. Ukrainian advocates are asking the NHL to sanction Alex Ovechkin . Kirill Marchenko had a good one-liner about his future, but is keeping mum on details. And Sportsnet asked the question—how will some of these long-term contracts age?

I have no stories, no more observations to share this morning. After I got home from camp around 5 p.m., I promptly handled some business, ate a hamburger with the crusts as buns because apparently I hadn't done any grocery shopping in over a week, and fell asleep by 7 p.m. Honestly, such a trivial annoyance as using the crusts made me laugh to myself. Life can't be too bad if that's the biggest annoyance, eh?

I am definitely not in hockey shape yet. But the eight hours were nice. So, let's do this hockey…

Pittsburgh Hockey Now: Evgeni Malkin . He either said, "I want to say yes" to playing another year, or "I won't say yes," but… It would mean the same. Malkin sounded a mature tone about his future and laid out the conditions under which he would want to play more years or retire. Evgeni Malkin held court .

What about Kris Letang ? Shelly Anderson had a chat with Letang and the future of the big three, too. Letang made a point of not being nostalgic about it .

Shells also talked with Filip Hallander about his future and what he's been through. Tell you what, Hallander looks pretty good in camp. Make no mistake, his journey and detour last season have made Hallander hungry .

PHN+: Two full days of observations and analysis, peppered with some of the conversations that I've had in the dressing room and reading between the lines. Come on back to PHN+—for a full accounting of Penguins training camp thoughts .

NHL Trade Talk, News, & National Hockey Now

NHLtraderumors.me: With some help from a Russian hockey writer, our buddy Dave Littman has the full story. Nikishin's agent indirectly blasted both Pierre LeBrun's report that Nikishin could return to the KHL and the Carolina Hurricanes for not trading Nikishin despite plenty of offers .

TSN: Ukrainian advocates aren't happy about Alex Ovechkin appearing in Vladimir Putin's political commercial and are asking the NHL to punish him for it .

We're in some real gray area here, aren't we? For the record, we have no plans to ask Malkin about any of this because, quite frankly, he's never taken a public stand. I don't know who tweeted it, but a media person suggested that if a player doesn't talk about politics, there's no reason to ask them about it. I like that standard. Ovechkin, however, has opened the door to being asked…

Sportsnet: The media giant referenced the Ville Koivunen contract as a bellwether, but didn't actually grade it. Instead, SN graded the deals that followed and which ones aren't going to age well .

The Athletic ($): Kirill Marchenko, the subject of so many trade rumors over the summer and reports that he won't sign in Columbus, did his preseason presser Friday. So, where does he want to play hockey? On the ice. Yep, he said it. Marchenko put on his tap shoes and danced around the hard questions but tried to be good to his teammates .

No, the Penguins can't steal Marchenko for merely second- and third-round picks, too.

Philly Hockey Now: Day 2 of Philly Flyers training camp. Will James has a good look at what's happening in Flyers camp .

Detroit Hockey Now: The lack of a GM in Detroit set contract negotiations back months with young defenseman Simon Edvinsson . But he's doing the team a solid and is in training camp without a new contract—but he had to sign a PTO?! Here's the scoop from Detroit Red Wings camp .

articles.title: Stephanie White divides Fever fans with controversial Caitlin Clark decision vs Tempo
articles.summary: A victory over the Toronto Tempo wasn’t enough to spare Indiana Fever head coach Stephanie White from some fan criticism. Returning from the international br...
articles.body:
A victory over the Toronto Tempo wasn't enough to spare Indiana Fever head coach Stephanie White from some fan criticism .

Returning from the international break, Stephanie White and the Indiana Fever didn't miss a beat, rolling to a 103-85 win over the Toronto Tempo.

Caitlin Clark picked up right where she left off, putting on a clinic in 34 minutes of action. She dropped 28 points, dished out 14 assists, and grabbed six rebounds, completely controlling the pace of the game. And that wasn't all, as Kelsey Mitchell broke the single-season WNBA scoring record with 33.

Stephanie White benches Caitlin Clark with 30 points and 10 assists on the line

Indiana Fever head coach Stephanie White has had her fair share of critics this season, but it can be unwarranted at times – often being used as a scapegoat.

However, a decision during the Fever's win over the Toronto Tempo caused a bit of controversy, as White benched Caitlin Clark when she was two points away from another 30 pt and 10+ assists game.

This caused a complete divide on social media.

One supporter made a very valid point: "She played 34 minutes!! We cannot risk injury before our toughest stretch and playoffs for a measly 2 points."

Another pointed out how many minutes she played: "She played 33 minutes. I don't think she was as thinking about 30 with a game on Sunday."

"No coach in their right mind should risk a star player this close to playoffs to stat pad. Horrible uneducated take." Said one supporter.

On the flip side, some fans weren't too pleased.

Someone claimed that the Fever didn't want to take the shine off Kelsey Mitchell: "I noticed that. My first thought was they want to let Kelsey shine alone on breaking the most points record. Surely, that's not the case."

Another blamed White: "Stephanie loves messing with CC's game. Imagine what Clark could do under the right coach."

"As much as I hate it too, it ain't worth her getting hurt." This fan was split.

It's worth keeping in mind that Clark still logged 34 minutes after being listed as probable with a back issue. Plus, when Stephanie White pulled her late in the fourth, she cleared out the whole bench—it was just a routine line change to sit the starters, not a personal benching.

articles.title: “Why Are Girls Mad?” – Sophie Cunningham Shares a Hot Take on Sydney Sweeney’s Controversial Novig Ad
articles.summary: Sydney Sweeney stirred the sporting world with a controversial ad for Novig. The prediction-market platform’s latest featured The Housemaid star in the most...
articles.body:
Sydney Sweeney stirred the sporting world with a controversial ad for Novig. The prediction-market platform's latest featured The Housemaid star in the most illicit way possible. While most of the female athletes across different sports were outraged, Sophie Cunningham certainly had a more mature take on the ad.

In a recent episode of her No Hesitation podcast , featuring Drew Hanlen, the WNBA star questioned, "Why are girls mad?" Defending Sweeney, the WNBA star further said, "That is literally what she does. Why is anyone mad? It is a gambling ad. Men, sports, pretty much naked women. Of course that's going to draw attention."

Cunningham said that it was 'morally weird' for her to agree with the ad. However, she believed that the girls in sports were 'powerful and strong' and they portray what it meant to be an athlete.

"I don't think the ad was coming for women in sport," the Indiana Fever star said and continued her praise for female athletes. Cunningham added, "I think it has been so cool to see girls. They're muscly, their thighs touch, they have broad shoulders, they might be taller than the average girl and probably the average boy."

Sophie Cunningham Understands Why Sydney Sweeney's Latest Ad Is Drawing Backlash

The Euphoria actress staying in controversy with a controversial ad isn't a new thing. Even American Eagle's jeans ad garnered enough negative remarks across industries. However, it still managed to lift up the sales for the company.

With strategically placed sports equipment to hide nudity, the Euphoria actress kind of slayed in the new Novig ad . Since the release, female athletes have voiced against her not-so-appropriate involvement in sports.

Sophie Cunningham, on the other hand, believes the Novig ad has nothing to do with women in sports. Although she understands why the ad is stirring the pot, the Fever guard supports Sydney Sweeney.

"I can understand when you first see that ad; it kind of deflates women. Because we've worked so hard to get a little bit of respect around here, but then when you really think about it, it's like, screw it! Let that girl [Sweeney] go do her thing."

"We can still say this has nothing to do with us. So, you know, it's nothing like everyone trying to hate on each other and figure out life. So, that's great."

Sweeney's latest Novig ad saw her almost naked with football, basketball, golf clubs, and tennis racquets strategically hiding the nudity. The most controversial part of the ad was the Once Upon a Time in Hollywood actress constantly repeating the word "sports."

articles.title: 5 Questions with Arrowhead Pride: does Indy stand a chance?
articles.summary: In Week 2 of 2026 our Indianapolis Colts will hit the road to take on the Kansas City Chiefs. Knowing the party was headed to KC, I sat down with Maurice Els...
articles.body:
In Week 2 of 2026 our Indianapolis Colts will hit the road to take on the Kansas City Chiefs . Knowing the party was headed to KC, I sat down with Maurice Elston of Arrowhead Pride , SB Nation's Chiefs blog. You can find him on Twitter @MrMauriceElston . We swapped questions and answers about both the Chiefs and Colts and what follows is what I've learned about this week's opponent.

Chris Shepherd: Based on Week 1, if you were an offensive coordinator tasked with creating a game plan to attack the Chiefs' defense, what would your plan look like? What areas of the field would you attack, what weaknesses would you target and how would you try to beat this Chiefs defense?

Maurice Elston: I would do anything possible to force Kansas City 's linebackers—primarily Nick Bolton—to cover in space or match up one-on-one. Bolton is an excellent run defender and the commander of the Chiefs' defense, but operating in coverage over a large area is not his greatest strength.

I would attack the middle of the field with tight ends and running backs, using motion and different formations to create favorable matchups against the linebackers. The Colts have a tight end in Tyler Warren who is capable of presenting that type of problem. Getting Warren matched against Bolton or another linebacker in space could give Indianapolis an opportunity to consistently move the football.

Chris Shepherd: In Week 1, Colts fans watched in horror as the Ravens moved Zay Flowers all over the field to exploit favorable matchups that the discombobulated Colts secondary never figured out how to adjust to. Do you think the Chiefs will try to exploit those same issues, and if so, who will Andy Reid and Eric Bieniemy slot into the Zay Flowers role for Kansas City?

Maurice Elston: I don't believe the Chiefs will copy Baltimore's strategy exactly because Kansas City doesn't have to lean on one receiver the way the Ravens leaned on Flowers. I absolutely expect Andy Reid and Eric Bieniemy to test the same communication problems Indianapolis experienced in Week 1, but they will likely do it with several different players.

The Chiefs can use motion, shifts and formations to create favorable matchups for Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, Travis Kelce and Kenneth Walker III. Instead of putting one player in the Flowers role, Kansas City can force the Colts to identify and communicate against multiple threats before the snap. That unpredictability could make the assignment even more difficult for Indianapolis' secondary.

Chris Shepherd: In Week 1, Patrick Mahomes made his return after recovering from last season's torn ACL. He completed 15 of 27 passes for 184 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. Did Mahomes look like the Patrick of old? Was he still the player who can take over games, or will he need some time to regain that form?

Maurice Elston: I wouldn't say Mahomes completely looked like his old self, but he did look healthy—and that was the most important thing Kansas City needed to see.

Mahomes demonstrated that his knee is fine, he can still scramble and he remains capable of making plays outside the pocket. From a passing standpoint, however, there was some understandable rust. He opened the game completing only two of his first 12 attempts and missed a few routine throws that we normally see him make.

He eventually settled down and completed 13 of his final 15 attempts, including two touchdown passes. Because he couldn't participate in his normal offseason routine and did not play during the preseason, some early rust should have been expected. He may not be completely back to his old form yet, but the second half showed that he is getting there.

Chris Shepherd: Can you give me one player on offense and one on defense whom Colts fans might not be familiar with but who you expect to make an impact Sunday night?

Maurice Elston: Offensively, I would watch rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen. He became one of the Chiefs' most talked-about young players during training camp and the preseason. Allen received only one target and did not record a catch in Week 1, but I expect Kansas City to begin incorporating him into the offense.

In my opinion, Allen may already be the best pure route runner in the Chiefs' wide receiver room. His ability to separate could become especially valuable against the man-to-man coverage Kansas City's receivers have consistently faced.

Defensively, I'll go with L'Jarius Sneed. It may seem strange to call Sneed an under-the-radar player considering what he has accomplished, but much of the attention surrounding Kansas City's secondary has focused on young outside cornerbacks Mansoor Delane and Nohl Williams.

Sneed's return to the slot gives Steve Spagnuolo a trusted defender who can cover, blitz and handle several different assignments. Having someone Spagnuolo trusts to lock down the slot changes what the Chiefs can do schematically, making Sneed an important piece of this defense even if he isn't receiving the most attention .

Chris Shepherd: How do you predict this game will play out? What does each team do well, where will they struggle and what is the final score?

Maurice Elston : I expect the Chiefs to win, although I don't anticipate the margin being as large as it was against Denver.

Indianapolis' best path to keeping the game close is through Jonathan Taylor and Tyler Warren. The Colts must remain committed to Taylor, stay ahead of the chains and use Warren to attack Kansas City's linebackers and safeties in coverage. There is no completely stopping Taylor because he is too talented, but if the Chiefs can contain him enough to force Indianapolis into third-and-long situations, Kansas City's pass rush and pressure packages can take control.

For the Colts defensively, the challenge will be handling Kansas City's motion, personnel groupings and improved running game without experiencing the communication breakdowns that hurt them against Baltimore. If those problems continue, Reid and Bieniemy will find ways to exploit them.

I believe Indianapolis keeps the game competitive for a while, but Kansas City eventually creates some separation and wins 24-14.

I can't thank Maurice enough for answering this week's questions. Make sure you head over to Arrowhead Pride and @MrMauriceElston on Twitter to check out his work.

articles.title: Former ESPN anchor smears Caitlin Clark fans with sweeping, false accusations of racism | Matt Calkins
articles.summary: Cari Champion called Caitlin Clark an "avatar" for hate and her fans MAGA on podcasts with Jemele Hill and Bakari Sellers, sparking fierce debate.
articles.body: Did you know that Caitlin Clark is an "avatar for people who want to spread hate"? Because Cari Champion does. Did you know that the fans who latched onto her are just middle Americans "who want to see White women do well in a sport that's traditionally Black"? THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Champion's all over that, too. The former ESPN anchor would also like you to know that Clark hasn't done enough to give Black players their respect, and that the WNBA is coddling Caitlin and her "MAGA" fans to the detriment of the league. She shared these insights in separate podcasts with Jemele Hill and Bakari Sellers. It was all very enlightening. And by enlightening I mean ridiculous. No doubt that Clark — the most popular women's basketball player ever — has displayed traits that warrant criticism. She can be petulant. She can be hostile toward refs. And she's about to lead the league in turnovers for the third consecutive season. But the racial narratives the media manufactures with her are as absurd as the maligning of her fan base. Who's really the hateful one here? Let's start with Champion's notion that Clark's fans are essentially country bumpkins looking for a white face to cheer for. This makes no sense. Sue Bird, Dianna Taurasi, Breanna Stewart, Sabrina Ionescu, and Kelsey Plum were all No. 1 overall picks who won the Wooden Award in their final year of college. All White — but none were selling out arenas. ELLE DUNCAN BLAMES CAITLIN CLARK, HER FANS FOR MEDIA SMEAR CAMPAIGN WHILE IGNORING FACTS That's because they weren't pulling up from 28 feet ten times a game en route to setting the all-time NCAA scoring record while leading the country in assists for three straight years. Clark didn't rise to fame because she played college basketball unlike any woman who's come before her, she did it because she played college hoops unlike any person had before. Given how popular athletes such as Serena Williams and Simone Biles were, it seems silly to think Clark wouldn't have achieved the same notoriety if she were Black. Plus, wasn't it LeBron James who posted "if you don't rock with Caitlin Clark's game you're just a FLAT OUT HATER!!!!!"? And isn't it Tyrese Haliburton who's a courtside regular at her Fever games? Could just be me, but those guys don't look very White. Next, there is Champion's assertion that Clark's fans are trying to "spread hate." Or that the league looks the other way when this "entitled" and "nasty" fan base "behaves like MAGA." She went so far as to say that Clark supporters can't accept other players' "queerness" or "blackness." Really? The source Clark detractors always cite is online vitriol, and there's no doubt that exists. But such vitriol never seems to be quantified in a way that's comparable to other famous athletes' fan bases. The unfortunate truth is that there are always going to be internet trolls who want to denigrate people behind their cat avatar on X. But are there any examples in which Clark fans crossed the line from online noise into real-world harassment? SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER In 2024, Brittney Griner said "I don’t appreciate the new fans that sit there and yell racial slurs at myself, my teammates and the people that I play against." But she provided no specifics or evidence to substantiate the claim, and though she didn’t single out Fever fans as the culprits, there was a strong implication that they were. Similarly, in May of last year, Angel Reese claimed that Fever fans hurled racist comments her way during a game. But after a review involving fans, team and arena staff and audio and video from the game, the WNBA said it could not substantiate the allegation. Does this mean it never happened? Not necessarily. But concrete evidence of Clark fans acting in a hateful manner — at least in real time — is severely lacking. What's not lacking, however, is the hostility toward Clark and her fans. Champion said that Clark being heterosexual, White and Catholic helped bring a new fan base that the WNBA is "coddling" for the sake of business. First of all, Clark being the most entertaining women's basketball player in the world is what brought in all those new fans — but could you imagine the inverse of that statement? That if a broadcaster bemoaned the "coddling" of a gay, Black and Muslim fan base? Instant cancellation. But Champion goes on. And she seems to disapprove of Clark not going out of her way to highlight Black players in a league that is 70 percent Black. She wishes Caitlin could be more like Wings point guard Paige Bueckers, who, in her 2021 ESPY's speech, said that Black women's basketball players were being overlooked. OK. Two things. 1)Every women's basketball player was being overlooked before Clark came on the scene. Her arrival elevated the popularity of players Black and White alike. 2) Could you imagine if a pundit said that Tiger Woods should do more to highlight his white peers in a white-dominated sport? Or that Shohei Ohtani should thank all the white players that came before him? Outrage would justifiably ensue. So let's stop with that idea. Sports leagues are not built on color. They are built on talent. Saying white players such as Clark or Bueckers should pay homage to their Black peers is as absurd as saying Steph Curry and Jalen Brunson should pay homage to their tall peers. It's about the individual. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD And if we're being honest here, Clark's race and sexual orientation may very well be working against her. Last year, after being called for a foul involving Clark, Griner was caught on camera saying what appeared to be "trash, f---ing White girl." Then, there was this year's All-Star voting, where Caitlin was ranked second among guards by the fans, third by the media....and 11th by the players. One might say this was pure jealousy, except that Kelsey Plum, who is also white and straight, finished sixth among fans, fifth among media and 12th among players. The year before, it went 6-6-16 for Plum. Most of us who follow Clark are aware of the hits she takes on the court, whether it's Chennedy Carter hip-checking her to the ground or Alyssa Thomas making closed-fist contact with her throat. But the hits are just as blatant from within press boxes or studios — and it's fair to question people's motivation. No one here is saying Caitlin or her supporters are above criticism. But all of Champion's rhetoric about Clark and her supposedly bigoted fan base? Some might see it as provocation. I can't help but wonder if it's projection.

articles.body: Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker remembered her late coach Jaspal Rana after carrying the Indian flag at the Asian Games 2026 opening ceremony on Saturday.Bhaker said she missed Rana during the ceremony, making the special occasion an emotional one. She carried the Indian flag alongside kabaddi star Pawan Sehrawat."Missed Jaspal sir a lot today, he was a flagbearer at the Asian Games. It was indeed an emotional day without his presence by my side," Bhaker said after the ceremony.Rana played key role in Bhaker’s careerRana, a former shooter and coach, died on June 11 at the age of 49. He played an important role in Bhaker’s career and guided her to two bronze medals at the 2024 Paris Olympics.Bhaker had earlier spoken about Rana’s influence on her approach to opening ceremonies at multi-sport events.Rana had told Bhaker that she could attend such ceremonies only if she was the flag-bearer. Otherwise, he wanted her to watch them on television because her competitions usually started soon after the opening ceremony.Rana’s advice made the moment more specialBhaker is competing at her third Asian Games. She missed the opening ceremony at her first Games in 2018 as she was based in Palembang, away from the main athletes’ village in Jakarta.She later attended the 2018 Commonwealth Games opening ceremony and recalled Rana’s advice to focus on her competition.That advice made Saturday’s occasion even more emotional as Bhaker herself walked out as one of India’s flag-bearers at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium.Bhaker’s focus now on shootingBhaker is the only athlete from independent India to win two medals at a single edition of the Olympics.She will now turn her attention to the shooting competition. articles.title: Aston Villa compound Tottenham’s misery despite Spurs ending goal drought
articles.summary: Unai Emery’s side get first league win of season with goals from Johan Manzambi, Nicolas Jackson and Emi Buendia.
articles.body:
48he end to Tottenham’s Premier League goal drought came too late as Aston Villa won 3-2 in north London to compound a miserable start for Roberto De Zerbi’s men.

Spurs remain without a league win this season and only netted their first goals of the campaign after the visitors had surged into a 3-0 lead on Saturday.

Villa had also struggled for goals themselves since the side that won the Europa League last season was torn apart during the transfer window.

But new signings Johan Manzambi and Nicolas Jackson struck either side of half-time to give Unai Emery’s new-look team their first league win before Emi Buendia’s wonder strike.

Even Tottenham’s first late consolation needed the aid of a Villa deflection when Conor Gallagher’s effort went in off Matty Cash before Jan Paul van Hecke headed home in stoppage time.

Spurs splashed out more than 300 million pounds ($400m) on new players to try and avoid a repeat of the battle for survival they endured last season.

Yet there remains little return on that investment.

In keeping with recent performances, Spurs started brightly before fizzling out.

Twice in a matter of seconds, Savio was kept out by Suzuki before the Japanese goalkeeper spread himself to turn behind Archie Gray’s powerful strike.

Villa had picked up just one point from their opening four league games but have missed their club record signing Manzambi for most of that period.

The Swiss international opened his Villa account when he tapped home Boubacar Kamara’s cross.

However, Tottenham will protest about new laws that force a player off the field for at least a minute after receiving treatment for an injury.

A head knock to centre-back Micky Van de Ven left them a man down at the back when Manzambi swept home.

Spurs only had themselves to blame for the second goal as van Hecke failed to deal with a long ball straight down the middle.

Jackson did well to evade the Dutch defender and then fired down into the ground and past Antonin Kinsky.

The Czech goalkeeper was powerless to stop Villa’s third 11 minutes from time when Buendia took aim from long range and brilliantly picked out the top corner.

A chorus of boos greeted Buendia’s strike as thousands of home fans headed for an early exit.

But those that left missed finally have something to celebrate.

Fine persistence from Mohammed Kudus teed up Gallagher to find the bottom corner via the outstretched foot of Cash.

Van Hecke then bulleted in from Andy Robertson’s free-kick with virtually the last touch of the game.

Spurs now must stew on another defeat for a three-week international break while rooted in the relegation zone.

Villa, by contrast, will hope victory can prove the catalyst to storm up the table as they did last season.

Emery’s men failed to win any of their first five league games a year ago, but ultimately finished fourth.

articles.body: A father and son who built their legacy in hammer throw shared one of the biggest moments of the Asian Games opening ceremony on Saturday.Japan’s Shigenobu Murofushi and his son Koji Murofushi jointly lit the cauldron at the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya, bringing the torch relay to a memorable end.Both Shigenobu and Koji are former Asian Games champions in hammer throw. The duo climbed the stairs to the podium together before lighting the cauldron.The ceremony featured dance, music and fireworks as the Asian Games officially opened in Aichi-Nagoya.From Olympic champion to father-son momentThe cauldron lighting was the final part of a relay involving some of Japan’s biggest sporting names.Women’s wrestler Fujinami Akari brought the torch into the stadium before passing it to four-time Olympic swimming champion Kitajima Kosuke.The torch then went to Ito Koji, a three-time gold medallist in athletics at the 1998 Bangkok Asian Games. Takahashi Ayaka, the 2016 Rio Olympics badminton women’s doubles champion, was next.The torch was then handed to Koji Murofushi, the 2004 Athens Olympics hammer throw champion.The final torchbearer was his father, Shigenobu Murofushi, who won the Asian Games hammer throw title five times in a row.The two then came together to light the cauldron, which had a metallic design inspired by the shape of a heart.Who is Shigenobu Murofushi?Shigenobu Murofushi is one of Japan’s most successful hammer throwers. He competed at three Olympic Games — Munich 1972, Montreal 1976 and Los Angeles 1984.He also served as Japan’s flag-bearer at the 1984 Olympics.Murofushi initially tried sumo and shot put before taking up hammer throw. In 1984, he set a Japanese record of 75.96m. That mark remained the national record until his son Koji broke it in 1998.Shigenobu won the Asian Games hammer throw gold medal in 1970, 1974, 1978, 1982 and 1986. He also won silver in 1966.His Asian Games medal record includes five gold medals and one silver.He also won gold at the 1979 and 1981 Asian Championships.Shigenobu’s Olympic journeyWhile Shigenobu dominated the Asian Games, an Olympic medal remained out of reach.He finished eighth at the 1972 Munich Olympics, 11th at Montreal 1976 and 15th at Los Angeles 1984.His son would later achieve what he could not at the Olympics.Koji Murofushi followed his father’s footstepsKoji started hammer throw at the age of 10 under the guidance of his father.He went on to become one of the leading hammer throwers in the world. Koji won the silver medal at the 2001 World Championships before claiming bronze in 2003.His biggest Olympic moment came at the 2004 Athens Games, where he won the hammer throw gold medal.He added an Olympic bronze at the 2012 London Games.Koji also became world champion in 2011 in Daegu.Koji’s Asian Games medal recordKoji continued his family’s success at the Asian Games.He won gold in hammer throw at Bangkok in 1998 and Busan in 2002. He had earlier won silver at Hiroshima in 1994.His Asian Games record therefore includes two gold medals and one silver.Koji also won gold at the 2002 Asian Championships and three silver medals at the continental championships in 1993, 1995 and 1998.A family legacy comes full circleThe Murofushis have now added another special chapter to their long sporting legacy.Shigenobu dominated the Asian Games in the 1970s and 1980s. Koji followed him into the event and later became an Olympic and world champion.On Saturday, the father and son stood together at the centre of the Asian Games opening ceremony — not to compete, but to light the flame that officially began the Games.Glittering opening ceremonyThe 20th Asian Games officially began in Nagoya with a two-hour opening ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium. Japan's Emperor Naruhito officially declared the Games open. Empress Masako, members of the Japanese imperial family, Olympic Council of Asia president Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani and International Olympic Committee president Kirsty Coventry were also present at the ceremony.The event started with the Japanese national anthem and the raising of the national flag. Nine members of the Japanese Self-Defence Forces carried the flag to the stage before it was hoisted.The stadium was then turned dark, with a spotlight focused on the Japanese flag.The ceremony was followed by the parade of athletes. Teams from 45 nations and regions took part, along with the OCA Refugee Team, taking the total number of participating delegations to 46.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Indian women's hockey team carrying World Cup mindset into Asian Games, says Deepika
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: KOLKATA: The night India’s Women’s Hockey World Cup dream ended in Amstelveen, Netherlands, sleep was hard to come by.Disappointment lingered in the d.
articles.body: KOLKATA: The night India’s Women’s Hockey World Cup dream ended in Amstelveen, Netherlands, sleep was hard to come by.Disappointment lingered in the dressing room, but according to drag-flicker Deepika Sehrawat, it was what happened next that revealed the character of this young Indian side. Four days later after suffering the heartbreak of missing out on the semifinals, the players regrouped, rallied around each other and signed off their campaign with a 3-1 victory over Germany, a response she believes holds the key to India’s Asian Games challenge.“My favourite memory is actually the last match,” Deepika told TOI from the team’s training base in Japan. “We had already gone out and everyone was disappointed after the match against Australia. Many of us probably didn’t sleep that night. But then everybody came together, focused on the next game and gave their best.”That ability to move on quickly from setbacks has become a defining trait of a squad that exceeded expectations at the World Cup, finishing fifth for its best result in 52 years.For Deepika, however, the biggest takeaway was neither tactical nor technical. “Many of us were playing our first World Cup, but we never felt like first-timers,” she said. “Everyone was supporting and motivating each other. The coaches also ensured there was no unnecessary pressure.”That same approach is guiding India’s preparations for the Asian Games, where a gold medal would secure direct qualification for Los Angeles Olympics, something they missed out on at the previous edition after losing to China in semifinals.China, the silver medallists at Paris Olympics, meanwhile, are once again expected to be among India’s toughest rivals, but Deepika insisted the squad is not looking too far ahead.“We had a team meeting and the message was very clear: take it one match at a time,” she said. “If we start thinking about a final before the tournament has even started, anything can happen. We want to keep the same mindset that we had at the World Cup.”The coaching staff has also used the period since the World Cup to address one of India’s biggest shortcomings — converting chances into goals. India’s defence stood firm against strong opponents, including England and Australia, but scoring remained an issue. Deepika said the team has since worked extensively on improving its attacking structure.“We weren’t creating enough chances and penalty corners,” she said. “A lot of work has gone into building attacks better, moving the ball from defence into the opposition half and making better decisions inside the circle.”For Deepika personally, preparations have included regular work with drag-flicking coach Taeke Taekema, an area where she shares responsibility with Navneet and the rest of the penalty-corner unit. “We’ve studied goalkeepers and opposition teams, and the coaches have been giving us inputs about areas we can target,” she said.The team has also carried over some of the rituals that became synonymous with its World Cup campaign, including the red-and-yellow strings worn by players throughout the tournament. “We’ve continued with it,” Deepika said. “What we started at the World Cup isn’t finished yet.”For a young squad preparing for one of the biggest tournaments of its careers, that sentiment perhaps captures the mood best. The World Cup journey may be over, but the belief it generated remains very much alive as India chase Asian Games gold and an Olympic berth.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: An update on the Cubs’ postseason odds and position
articles.summary: Here’s where the Cubs stand with eight games remaining in the regular season.
articles.body:
Eight games remain in the 2026 regular season.

Entering Saturday's action, the Cubs , Phillies and Padres are all tied for the three National League wild card spots at 85-69. The Diamondbacks are 80-74 and on the verge of elimination, five games behind; their elimination number with the Cubs is 3. (It's more complicated for Arizona with the Phillies and Padres, but for now let's skip that.)

This is where it's really fortunate that the Cubs have the tiebreaker over both those teams. If all three teams wound up tied at the end of the regular season, the Cubs would get the first wild card spot. In that scenario they'd host the Phillies, because Philadelphia swept their season series 6-0 over San Diego . Here are all the various tiebreaker rules.

Today, The Athletic posted an article noting the odds and percentages for various postseason scenarios and so I thought it'd be useful for us to take a look at them.

First, here are the percentage odds for the possible postseason matchups for the first two rounds:

As you can see, the wild card round is still kind of muddled. The most likely matchup for the Cubs is still with the Phillies, but it's possible they could face the Padres — or even the Braves, if the Cubs get dumped into the last wild card spot, the No. 6 seed.

The Brewers are very likely to be the No. 1 National League seed. They currently lead the Dodgers by two games and hold the tiebreaker.

Now, here are the Cubs' percentages of making the postseason and where they would wind up, based on each possible W/L record:

The best-case scenario here would be for the Cubs to go at least 6-2 in the eight remaining games. That would give them an 89 percent or better chance of being the top wild card team and hosting the wild card series. Even at 5-3, they would be more likely than not to be the host team, depending on what the other teams involved do over the same span.

The worst-case scenarios are going 2-6 or worse, which could dump them into the No. 6 position. And an 0-8 run (which would actually be 0-9, since the Cubs lost Friday) would give them a small chance (10 percent) of missing the postseason completely.

I don't think that "worst case" is going to happen. I still think the Cubs will take the last two games in Cincinnati and then they've got the Marlins at home. Miami is 31-45 on the road this year and so the Cubs ought to take at least two of three from them at Wrigley Field. Then the Cubs travel to Boston , where the Red Sox are likely going to be locked in to the second wild card spot in the American League before that series begins. So the Cubs should win at least one, maybe two, at Fenway Park.

That would leave the Cubs at either 5-3 or 6-2 in the eight remaining games, giving them good odds of being the host team for a Wild Card series at Wrigley Field.

Fingers crossed. As always, we await developments.

articles.title: George Russell praised for honest admission about Kimi Antonelli's F1 form
articles.summary: David Coulthard has praised George Russell for publicly admitting that Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli is currently outperforming him as the 2026 title sli...
articles.body:
Former Formula 1 driver David Coulthard has praised George Russell for admitting that his Mercedes team-mate and current championship leader Kimi Antonelli is doing a better job.

Antonelli secured his eighth victory of the season at the inaugural Spanish Grand Prix at the new Madring circuit, extending his lead in the standings to 81 points over Russell, who sits second. Russell, meanwhile, salvaged a fifth-place finish.

The British driver arrived at the season-opening Australian Grand Prix as one of the favourites for the title. But after winning in Melbourne and the subsequent sprint race in China, he watched his title hopes slip away as Antonelli claimed win after win.

Speaking on the Up To Speed podcast, 13-time grand prix winner Coulthard commended Russell for being honest in media sessions about the fact that his team-mate is currently doing a better job than he is.

"I think what we're just seeing is, in the same way that this year's formula has suited Lewis [Hamilton] more relative to Charles [Leclerc], there's been a swing in their performance from last year to this year," he said.

"Oscar [Piastri] has dropped off form relative to Lando [Norris], where he was leading the world championship up until Baku last year. So, it's swings and roundabouts of this formula.

"We've got Kimi coming alive and George is on the ropes. But in fairness to George, I think he's come to terms with it. He's fronting up to the media. He's answering the questions.

"He did an interview with Martin Brundle over the weekend where he said, 'Look, Kimi is just doing a better job than me right now.' I think that's a big man who can admit that publicly.

"We would all be thinking it, but sometimes racing drivers bury their heads in the sand, and it's just one excuse after another. But I believe in George. I feel for him. It's a championship that's slipping away, but he's still young enough in his career that he'll have his moment."

articles.title: 2026 OKC Thunder fan survey results: Cason Wallace should be 5th starter
articles.summary: 2026 Oklahoma City Thunder fan survey results: Cason Wallace should be 5th starter.
articles.body:
With the 2026-27 regular season right around the corner, the Oklahoma City Thunder enter the year as a popular title pick. Even after their summer of cost-cutting moves, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Chet Holmgren and Jalen Williams remain one of the most successful and decorated trios in the league.

The Thunder had a league-best 64-18 this past regular season. But fell short of their back-to-back ambitions in the 2026 Western Conference Finals. Injuries played a large part in that. But that's in the past. Can't change anything about it now.

Now that the offseason is behind us and we're looking ahead to another nine-month marathon, let's rewind on OKC's biggest moves and preview what most folks believe the Thunder will do this upcoming year.

To get ready for the upcoming season, Thunder Wire conducted a 16-question fan survey . A total of 1,145 Thunder fans participated. Not every question was answered, though. The response totals for each question can be seen in the top-left corner of the pie charts.

One question was about who should be OKC's fifth starter. Everybody knows four of the five Thunder starters. It'll be Gilgeous-Alexander, Williams, Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein. But the fifth? Up for grabs. Lu Dort was traded this offseason. He was a seven-year starter. Most fans think it'll be Cason Wallace.

That makes the most sense. Like John Stewart with Hal Jordan, Wallace learned under Dort for three years. And as the pseudo-sixth starter, it'd be the most seamless promotion. The 22-year-old is ready to add more to his plate. Being named a full-time starter is one of the easiest ways to do that.

You want your best perimeter defender to start games. That's how you match minutes with the opposition's best scorers. Starting Wallace gives OKC that option. He's also fine as an off-ball player. He should get funneled plenty of catch-and-shoot looks from the outside.

Mitchell is the other popular choice. But he's better suited to a Sixth Man role. He enjoyed a breakout last year as a 14-point scorer. He stepped up in the 2026 NBA playoffs as well. Running the second-unit offense will give him the keys to the car whenever Gilgeous-Alexander is catching a breather.

Now, I think Wallace should start over Mitchell. But that doesn't necessarily mean he should close over him, too. I think it'll be on a game-by-game basis. Some clutch situations will require your top perimeter defender; others will require another go-to scorer. Heck, both could be on the floor as OKC could opt for just one center.

Starting in the NBA is always a prestigious honor. And I think Wallace starting over Mitchell makes the most strategic sense, too. That said, it doesn't mean the Thunder are prioritizing one over the other. Think we'll see how that plays out in the 2026-27 regular season. Both are due for huge upgrades in role and responsibilities.

articles.title: Rece Davis expresses one regret about Ted Cruz interview on ‘College GameDay’
articles.summary: Last Saturday, Rece Davis interviewed Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) for nearly 10 minutes on ESPN’s College GameDay, live from Austin, Texas. Cruz co-authored the...
articles.body:
Last Saturday, Rece Davis interviewed Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) for nearly 10 minutes on ESPN's College GameDay , live from Austin, Texas. Cruz co-authored the Protect College Sports Act , a bipartisan bill aiming to shift power back to the NCAA and universities in response to the NIL and player empowerment boom.

The legislation is nuanced and tedious, but the backlash to Cruz's GameDay appearance has been plain as day.

Cruz was relentlessly booed for the duration of his GameDay segment, and everyone from the NAACP and Bomani Jones reprimanded ESPN for its slanted coverage of the Protect College Sports Act.

On Friday, Kirk Herbstreit pleaded apolitical and claimed he didn't know anything about Cruz, which drew even more intense backlash . Davis also offered his perspective to Mississippi Today ahead of GameDay taking over Ole Miss's campus on Saturday morning.

When asked about GameDay 's responsibility to platform dissenting voices, Davis expressed one regret from his interview with Cruz.

"We asked him a question about some of the things, like compensation ," Davis said. "In a longer forum, of course they do. I mean, you have to present both sides of it. And I think that we've had a number of people on our air, not necessarily just on that show, but over the years — you don't have to look very far to find people who have been critical of this legislation."

"In that instance, I would love to have gotten to another question representing the other side to hear his response on it," Davis continued. "But at the same time, I don't think that we wanted to turn the whole show into crossfire. It was a timely situation. He was on, and you know, it is what it is."

Read Davis's full comments about the controversial ordeal below.

"People are going to criticize anytime you do anything that touches politics, and this is political, though not partisan, because there's pending legislation. So, we thought it was a good opportunity to bring him on to talk about it since they were about to vote. I understand that some people would rather hear about football. We'd rather talk about football. We wish all these issues were easily solved and not on the forefront. But I think anytime you have something that is going to be as impactful on the sport as potentially this legislation could be — I'm not endorsing it. I am very familiar with it. I have some questions about it. A couple that I would like to have gotten to, one that I did get to, that are reasonable oppositions to this. At the same time, I think the need for structure is important. He, along with Democratic Senator Maria Cantwell, they put forward this legislation. My sense of it is that the reaction was largely due to partisan politics, at least certainly there, and not necessarily a reaction to that particular piece of bipartisan legislation. Doesn't mean everybody supports it. A lot of people that I respect greatly and are very close to me, and I've talked about it extensively with [them], have really significant reservations about it. articles.title: How coaching at Butler helped prepare Brad Stevens to run the Boston Celtics
articles.summary: "Trying to build teams at Butler was by far the best thing to help me in this role," said Stevens.
articles.body:
In a lot of ways, trying to run a mid-major college basketball team can b a lot like being an NBA executive. You have to put the players on the roster via a strong and coherent plan for the program, signing prospects and developing them into elite players for the level they will be at, and then see them leave as they age out of the program or find better opportunities elsewhere.

And Boston Celtics President of Basketball Operations Brad Stevens broke down how his time caching Butler helped prepare him to take over the reigns from Celtics legend Danny Ainge in his current role during a recent interview on Frank Isola and Brian Scalabrine's "The Starting Lineup" show on SiriusXM NBA Radio. "Trying to build teams at Butler was by far the best thing to help me in this role," said Stevens (h/t the Boston Globe's Chad Finn ).

"Because, you talk about the last few years, we have to find guys that, for whatever reason, are now minimums and we have to hopefully put them in a position to soar with their strengths and really take that next leap in their career," he added. "We're not going to get the first pick at Butler, you know?"

"And when we were recruiting there, there were challenges because you weren't going to beat Indiana and Purdue and all those teams for players," said the Celtics president. "You just had to find the right fits for you."

"And I think that that's kind of the same way when you're up against the aprons and all that stuff, so it was a great education."

articles.title: Mohammad Rizwan gambling and betting allegations: Pakistan star knocks on ICC door amid NCCIA investigation
articles.summary: With PCB investigating Mohammad Rizwan over gambling and betting allegations, the Pakistan star asks for help from ICC.
articles.body:
Pakistan star Mohammad Rizwan has approached the ICC's Anti-Corruption Unit for procedural clarity amid an NCCIA investigation.

The move follows the Lahore High Court rejecting his petition challenging the agency's jurisdiction.

No findings of wrongdoing have been announced against Rizwan or Imam-ul-Haq at this stage.

Mohammad Rizwan asks for help from the ICC

Mohammad Rizwan's turbulent few weeks since Pakistan's tour of England have escalated into an international governance question, with the wicketkeeper-batter now seeking answers directly from cricket's global anti-corruption authority.

It marks a significant shift for a player who, across more than a decade and close to 250 international appearances, had never previously faced allegations connected to illegal betting or gambling.

The move follows a setback in Pakistan's domestic courts. Rizwan had approached the Lahore High Court to challenge the jurisdiction of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency to investigate him at all, but Chief Justice Aalia Neelum declined to intervene, directing him instead to respond to the agency's notice through the established process.

His lawyer, Qazi Umair Ali, had argued in that hearing that the ICC's Anti-Corruption Unit, not a domestic cybercrime agency, was the appropriate forum for any corruption-related allegation involving an international cricketer.

With that argument rejected domestically, Rizwan has now taken the same underlying question to the ICC itself, seeking clarity on whether cricket's own anti-corruption machinery was ever engaged in a process that has already seen his mobile phone seized, transported from England to Pakistan, and subjected to forensic examination.

What Mohammad Rizwan has asked the ICC to clarify

According to Geo News , Rizwan submitted his request through the ICC ACU's online portal, and the approach has been described as a request for procedural guidance rather than a formal complaint against any individual or organisation.

Specifically, he has asked whether the ICC's Anti-Corruption Unit or the England and Wales Cricket Board's own anti-corruption authorities were aware of, or involved in, the seizure of his phone while he was in England.

He has also sought guidance on his own responsibilities should he be required to cooperate with anti-corruption investigators again in future, alongside asking whether the entire chain of custody, from the seizure itself through to the cross-border transfer and forensic analysis, complied with the ICC's own Anti-Corruption Code.

Under that code, if any player from a member country is suspected of a breach, the ICC's unit is meant to conduct its own inquiry and keep the relevant board informed throughout.

Whether that protocol was followed in Rizwan's case remains genuinely unclear. PTI has reported that it is not established whether the PCB itself formally suspects Rizwan of any wrongdoing, or whether it notified the ICC ACU of the matter at any stage, a gap in the public record that sits at the heart of what Rizwan is now asking the governing body to clarify.

It is worth restating plainly what has and has not happened here. The NCCIA has not announced any conclusion establishing that Rizwan or Imam-ul-Haq engaged in illegal betting, gambling or corrupt cricketing activity, and Geo News reported earlier this week that an initial examination of the seized phones had not revealed anything significant, even as a deeper forensic process continues.

The investigation originated from allegations of dressing-room information leaks during Pakistan's tour, with investigators also examining financial transactions around the same period, but no formal finding of misconduct has been made public against either player.

Why the procedural question matters regardless of the eventual outcome

Rizwan's approach to the ICC is a sensible one on its own terms, since a player facing scrutiny of this nature has every right to understand which body has jurisdiction and whether the correct chain of process was followed before his personal device was seized and sent abroad for analysis.

That question would matter even if the investigation ultimately clears him entirely, because a flawed process undermines confidence in the outcome either way. The wider concern is one of transparency rather than guilt or innocence.

A domestic cybercrime agency taking the lead on what appears, at least in part, to be a cricket integrity matter, without clarity on whether the sport's own anti-corruption unit was ever looped in, is an unusual arrangement that Pakistan's board has yet to explain publicly.

Until the PCB or the ICC clarifies exactly how this investigation has been run, the procedural questions Rizwan is asking are likely to attract as much attention as whatever the NCCIA eventually concludes.

articles.title: Robin Raikkonen’s rise earns comparison with Max Verstappen’s early journey
articles.summary: David Coulthard has drawn parallels between Robin Raikkonen's early motorsport journey and the path followed by Max Verstappen under the close guidance of hi...
articles.body:
David Coulthard has drawn parallels between Robin Raikkonen's early motorsport journey and the path followed by Max Verstappen under the close guidance of his father, Jos, during his formative years.

As has been known for several days, Red Bull has strengthened its ranks by bringing the son of former McLaren, Ferrari, Lotus and Alfa Romeo driver Kimi Raikkonen into its junior programme at just 11 years old, with young Robin already making a name for himself in karting.

Speaking on the Up to Speed podcast, the former F1 driver highlighted Robin Raikkonen's strong progress in karting and the commitment shown by his family, who have moved from Switzerland to Italy to allow him to train close to the karting circuit.

Coulthard compared this approach to the way Jos Verstappen supported Max during his early career, while also pointing out that success in karting does not necessarily translate directly to success in single-seaters due to the significant differences between the two types of machinery.

"He's doing brilliantly in karting. The family have committed. They've moved from Switzerland to Italy to live by the kart track. He'll be driving every day," the former McLaren driver said.

"He is doing what Jos Verstappen did with Max. They are developing, let's say, the perfect scenario for the most experienced young driver. One thing I'll say, though, some of the best karters never make it in cars because it's a different vehicle dynamic. It's a solid chassis. There's no suspension. It's got a solid rear axle. When you go to a car, you have suspension, you have a differential, you have downforce."

He also praised Robin's current performances in karting and the way he has been brought up, noting that the young driver appears grounded despite already enjoying success. The former F1 driver believes his family environment will help keep him grounded, although he stressed that Robin is still only a child and that his character and approach could change as he grows older, particularly during adolescence.

Coulthard warns Raikkonen's son faces crucial test as he grows up

"The kid is winning in karting. He seems like a really nice kid, because some kids you can already see there's a bit of arrogance there. I see all sorts of my journey around the world, and his parents are grounded. So, he's going to be grounded. Let's see how he is when he becomes a young man. He's a boy right now. When he goes through puberty, that's when things change."

Finally, Coulthard stressed that the real test will come as Robin grows older, when it becomes clear whether he can maintain the focus, determination and talent needed to cope with the setbacks that are an inevitable part of motorsport. He noted that even the most successful drivers experience far more defeats than victories, with Lewis Hamilton serving as a clear example after competing in hundreds of Grands Prix throughout his career.

"Kids change, and that's when you find out whether they've still got the focus and they've got the determination and the talent and the need for the constant pain of failure. Or hopefully not constant, but there's more failure in motor racing than there is success.

"Lewis is the most winning driver in terms of grand prix victories, but he's done 400-odd grands prix. He's lost 300-odd grands prix. He's only won 100-odd. So, there's a lot of pain there."

articles.title: Cowboys vs Commanders: 3 reasons to love the matchup in Week 2
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys host the Washington Commanders in an NFC East clash during Week 2, here are three reasons to love the matchup for the Cowboys.
articles.body:
The season didn't start off on the right foot for the Dallas Cowboys , but they don't have time to sulk. Another rival is next on the schedule and Brian Schottenheimer's team cannot afford to go 0-2 by losing to the Washington Commanders at home.

Losing your first two games would be bad, but it would be made worse if they lost two NFC East games, putting the Cowboys well behind in the division early in the year. However, there are some silver linings for the Cowboys as they will be home and they are taking on a Commanders team that doesn't appear to be very good. Here are three things to love about hosting the Commanders in Week 2.

If you haven't been keeping score at home, we'll fill you in, Prescott is 13-2 in his career against the Commanders, which includes a perfect 7-0 at home. More astoundingly, Prescott has thrown 20 touchdowns, against zero interceptions in games at AT&T Stadium against the Washington franchise.

Those are impressive numbers and Prescott needs to assert more dominance over the Commanders to ensure the Cowboys don't get off to a 0-2 start. The team and Prescott's streak over the New York Giants came to an unceremonious end last week, that cannot happen in back-to-back weeks.

The Commanders have a young quarterback who they hope will turn into a star, but they haven't surrounded him with elite weapons. Jayden Daniels is throwing to Terry McLaurin , who just turned 30 years old and is coming off a rough season, and Stefan Diggs, who is 32 and didn't sign with the Commanders until training camp in August . Additionally, WR Antonio Williams had a solid debut, but he's still a rookie learning his way.

Those are solid WRs, but not a top trio, which could limit the Commanders' passing game.

Daniels and the running game had a good start to their season last week, but it wasn't an explosive rushing attack. They averaged just 4.1 yards a carry and didn't have a run over 14 yards.

The Commanders' offense didn't look good through three quarters against the Philadelphia Eagles but did rally late once they got desperate. If Christian Parker's defense can play better in Week 2, they should be able to slow down an offense that doesn't have a lot of play making ability.

The Commanders were one of the worst defensive teams in the league last year, and although they did show improvement in their Week 1 loss, they could be without their leader against the Cowboys. Linebacker Frankie Luvu is in danger of missing the Week 2 matchup with a groin strain.

If Luvu doesn't play, the Commanders will lose one of their best defenders. The veteran LB does a little of everything for Dan Quinn's defense, Luvu had 86 tackles, five for a loss, three sacks and six passes defended last season.

The Commanders don't have much LB depth behind Luvu, so if he doesn't play, expect the Cowboys to attack his backup, either third-year man Jordan Magee or offseason addition Leo Chenal will fill the void. If Luvu does play, it's fair to wonder if he's 100% in the matchup. Luvu's health status does give the Cowboys an edge heading into Week 2.

articles.title: Joe Burrow’s status and top Bengals vs. Texans things to know
articles.summary: Bengals vs. Texans storylines and notes to know before Week 2 starts.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals attempt to make it a 2-0 start to the season by going to Houston and picking up a win over the Texans in Week 2.

Important thing, too, considering what looms right after: A trip to Pittsburgh for another dance with the Steelers.

Easier said than done, though, especially with some major questions chasing the Bengals out of the season opener. Joe Burrow 's health is one thing. Other items include some lagging parts of his offense and questions around a rebuilt defense.

This felt like the big Chase Brown breakout year, especially as he plays for a new contract. Brown had 56 yards and a score during the win over Tampa Bay in the opener, but on a 3.5 per-carry average. He caught five of six targets for 22 yards. The offense needs better balance and Brown is a big part of that. Depth behind him is thin, too. Working behind the best line of the Burrow era, Bengals coaches need to find a way to get the dynamic Brown going so Houston's pass-rush stays honest.

Shemar Stewart is back after recovering from a training camp injury that, at first, looked like it could be severe enough to end his season. That stroke of good fortune means he gets to join a front seven that helped force four turnovers in Week 1. How he fits in the rotation with the likes of Myles Murphy , Boye Mafe and Cashius Howell remains to be seen. He's got the pass-rushing juice to help and can kick inside to ease some pressure on the middle in different formations, though, so it's interesting to watch.

Amarius Mims looks like an All-Pro after flashing hints of it as last season concluded and now after the Week 1 dominance. But the Texans are no easy task: Will Anderson Jr. , Mario Edwards Jr. and Jadeveon Clowney all got on the board with at least half-sacks in Week 1. DeMeco Ryans ' defensive-minded ways produce nasty fronts that are deep with pressure creators, so Mims faces a far bigger task than Week 1. If he's up to it without much help, it means the Bengals can shift help in other directions.

Barring an absolute stunner, all signs point to Joe Burrow playing as normal against the Texans . The Bengals had to list him as "questionable" on the final injury report because "probable" doesn't really exist anymore. Back injuries/discomfort can be tricky, but Burrow publicly ramped up to normal usage by the end of the week. Still, it's something to watch before the game. And once that back starts taking hits, if any, we'll see how Burrow's throwing motion and overall comfort level look. For now, no reason for concern. But given the history, nobody can fault Bengals fans for how they'll be feeling all day Sunday.

articles.title: Rangers add Otanez, option Ahlstrom
articles.summary: The Rangers brought in a fresh arm for the pen on Friday
articles.body:
The Texas Rangers purchased the contract of righthanded pitcher Michel Otanez prior to Friday's game against the Toronto Blue Jays . To make room for Otanez on the active roster, the Rangers optioned lefthanded pitcher Robbie Ahlstrom to AAA Round Rock. To make room for Otanez on the 40 man roster, the Rangers transferred pitcher Cole Winn from the 15 day injured list to the 60 day injured list.

The Rangers' starters have not been going deep into games of late, and with the usage of the bullpen in the Boston series, the Rangers opted to get a fresh arm up. I had thought that Ahlstrom, who has struggled of late and pitched on Thursday, would be sent down in favor of Winston Santos, who would give the Rangers a multi-inning guy for length in case of a blowout.

Instead, Texas opted for Otanez, who had been claimed on waivers by the Rangers this winter, but who was designated for assignment in June, cleared waivers, and was outrighted. The 29 year old has an unimpressive 4.42 in 55 innings over 50 appearances for Round Rock this season, with 74 Ks against 42 walks, but since a 5 run outing in Tacoma in late June, Otanez has a 1.33 ERA in 27 innings, with 35 Ks and 13 walks. It may be he's turned a corner.
