articles.title: Saracens 2026-27 Season Prediction: A Return To The PREM Playoffs
articles.summary: FloRugby predicts where Saracens will finish in the 2026-27 Gallagher PREM and whether Brendan Venter can turn them into title contenders.
articles.body:
Saracens F.C. enter 2026-27 as a contender with an unusually strong case for improvement.

They finished fifth in the Gallagher PREM last season at 10-8 with 57 points, missing the playoffs by six points, yet posted the league's second-best point differential at +179 and scored 628 points, third most.

Now Brendan Venter has replaced Mark McCall as director of rugby, while Tomos Williams, George Martin and Alfie Barbeary headline a substantial roster reshuffle. Saracens have championship-level talent, but also new combinations, a tighthead question and the same challenge that undermined 2025-26: turning dominance into wins.

The evidence points toward a playoff return, but not necessarily first place.

Why Saracens Should Climb Back Into The Top Four

The strongest argument for improvement is that Saracens already performed like a better team than fifth place.

Their +179 differential trailed only Bath's +222 and exceeded Northampton's +157, Exeter's +154 and Leicester's +178. Saracens also scored 628 points, behind only Northampton and Bath. Entering the final round, they led the PREM with 155 turnovers won and 51 tackle turnovers.

Those numbers suggest Saracens do not need a tactical reconstruction. Their pressure game remained disruptive, and their attack produced plenty.

The offseason could improve two important areas. Williams replaces Ivan van Zyl at scrum-half and gives Saracens more attacking threat around the ruck. Pairing his ability to accelerate play with Owen Farrell's territory and game control creates an intriguing halfback combination.

Martin, meanwhile, gives Saracens an England lock who can add major collision power alongside Maro Itoje. With Ben Earl, Juan Martín González and Barbeary available in the back row, the first-choice pack still looks capable of matching leading PREM opponents.

Venter also inherits considerable coaching continuity beneath him. Joe Shaw remains head coach, with Ian Peel, Adam Powell, Dan Vickers, Rob Webber and Dai Flanagan still part of the structure. This is a leadership transition, not a complete reset.

The case against Saracens begins with a warning: underlying numbers do not automatically become wins.

They lost eight league matches last season. Bath beat them 62-15 in March, Northampton followed with a 21-17 victory at The Showdown, and Exeter ended Saracens' four-match winning streak with a 32-12 victory in the regular-season finale.

That inconsistency must be fixed rather than dismissed as bad fortune.

There has also been substantial turnover. Tom Willis, Theo McFarland, Marco Riccioni, Alex Lozowski and van Zyl are among 16 confirmed departures across the senior and senior-academy groups. Williams, Martin and Barbeary are significant additions, but replacing established combinations can take time.

The domestic competition is unforgiving. Northampton are defending champions, Bath finished second with the league's best differential, and Exeter and Leicester also finished above Saracens. Returning to the top four requires overtaking at least one proven playoff team.

The Swing Factor: Can The Tighthead Rotation Hold Up?

Saracens' most important positional uncertainty is tighthead prop.

Riccioni has departed, and the planned signing of Jermain Ainsley collapsed when his agreement was terminated for personal reasons. Ainsley will not join Saracens.

That leaves Alec Clarey, Marcus Street, new signing Corné Weilbach and younger options responsible for a position that can become decisive against championship-level packs.

Elsewhere, Saracens have obvious depth. Itoje and Martin can start at lock with Nick Isiekwe and Hugh Tizard behind them. Theo Dan and Jamie George offer two established hooker options. Earl, González, Barbeary and Andy Onyeama-Christie allow multiple back-row configurations.

If Clarey, Street and Weilbach provide stable set-piece performances, Saracens' pack has the talent to become a major strength. If the scrum becomes vulnerable or injuries expose the rotation, opponents will have a clear place to attack.

That could separate a top-two championship challenge from another fight around fourth or fifth.

Saracens' Best And Worst Realistic Outcomes

The realistic ceiling is a PREM championship.

That requires Venter to restore week-to-week efficiency, Williams to improve the attack's tempo, Martin to strengthen the pack and Barbeary to replace enough of Willis' overall contribution. Noah Caluori returning strongly from wrist surgery would add another attacking weapon after his 18-try PREM breakthrough in 2025-26.

Saracens do not need every variable to become perfect to contend. Their performances last season already included a 20-14 Champions Cup victory over Toulouse and an extraordinary 85-19 league win at Sale. The ceiling is established.

A top-two finish followed by a championship is plausible.

The realistic floor is fifth or sixth. New combinations could take longer than expected, front-row depth could become exposed and international workloads could bite. Most importantly, Saracens could continue producing excellent aggregate statistics without becoming reliable enough in decisive matches.

Another season outside the playoffs would be a major disappointment.

Saracens will compete in the Investec Champions Cup, with Connacht, Toulouse, the 10bet Lions and Stade Rochelais their playable Pool 2 opponents.

Last season they beat Clermont and Toulouse at home in Europe but lost away to the Sharks and Glasgow before Bath eliminated them 31-22 in the Round of 16.

A Round-of-16 appearance should be the minimum expectation in 2026-27. Reaching a quarterfinal is realistic, while a semifinal or final would require the consistency Saracens are trying to rediscover domestically.

Competing seriously on both fronts will also test their prop depth and player management.

Saracens are a likely playoff team and genuine championship contender, but third is the strongest preseason call.

Their realistic regular-season range is second through fifth. The argument for placing them above fifth is compelling: last season's second-best point differential, third-ranked scoring output and exceptional turnover production all suggest their performance level was better than their record. Williams and Martin could improve important parts of an already talented side.

Predicting first would go too far. Northampton enter as defending champions, Bath produced the league's best differential, and both Exeter and Leicester proved capable of finishing above Saracens last season. Saracens themselves are integrating major personnel changes under a new director of rugby while carrying a real question at tighthead.

Third accounts for both sides of the evidence. It predicts that Venter improves Saracens' conversion of good performances into victories without assuming every problem disappears immediately.

The prediction will look too pessimistic if Williams transforms the halfback dynamic, the scrum holds and Saracens rediscover the ruthless closing ability associated with their championship teams. Under those conditions, they can finish top two and win the PREM.

It will look too optimistic if tighthead becomes a weekly vulnerability and last season's inconsistency proves structural rather than temporary.

The most likely outcome is a top-four return, a PREM semifinal and a Champions Cup knockout run with quarterfinal potential. Saracens have enough talent to win the championship, but third place is the call because 2026-27 should first mark their return to the playoffs before anyone assumes Venter's new version of Saracens is already another finished winning machine.

articles.title: Raiders Mailbag: Will Rob Leonard dial up more blitzes in Las Vegas’ Week 2 matchup against Los Angeles Chargers?
articles.summary: Returning Raider Nation’s questions for the week
articles.body:
The 24-hour rule has long passed, meaning it's time to put the Las Vegas Raiders ' Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins behind us and start focusing on the Week 2 matchup against a familiar AFC West foe: the Los Angeles Chargers . To help preview the game, let's get into this week's mailbag!

Q: Do you think Rob Leonard dials up the pressure this week and goes after the Chargers' IOL? O/U 45% blitz rate for this one?

A: I'll take the under on 45 percent because only two teams — the Vikings (mad man Brian Flores at over 80%) and Commanders (50.9%) — were above that mark in Week 1, according to Ryan Paganetti on X/Twitter . Granted, the Jets (44.9%), Ravens (43.4%) and Lions (43.0%) were pretty close to the number. Meanwhile, the Raiders blitzed just 24.0% of the time against Miami, which ranked 18th across the league.

Could Leonard dial up the heat more in Los Angeles ? Sure, and I think you're onto something about the Chargers' interior offensive line, which is the weakest part of their roster. With free-agent signing Tyler Biadasz out for the year, they have a rookie center in Jake Slaughter, meaning the Bolts have a young lineman making his second NFL start in the position that typically helps set the protection scheme.

Having a veteran quarterback like Justin Herbert helps with that, but the Shanahan coaching tree (which L.A.'s new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is a branch of) typically likes to have the center set the protection to take that off the quarterback's plate. It sounds like McDaniel has adjusted with Biadasz's injury, since Jim Harbaugh said this week that Herbert calls the team's protections (h/t ESPN's Kris Rhim ). But it's still a new offense that doesn't have a veteran center as a fail-safe if things aren't going well.

Circling back to the question, given the Chargers' weakness up front, I think it's safe to assume Leonard will at least give them a variety of looks at the beginning of the game and adjust later on if needed. However, I wouldn't be surprised if the actual blitz rate (rushing five or more defenders) stays pretty consistent.

Instead, I'd expect to see more simulated pressures where the Raiders give a blitz look pre-snap and have an off-ball linebacker ( Quay Walker or Nakobe Dean ) rush the passer while a lineman ( Malcolm Koonce , Kwity Paye or one of the defensive tackles) drops into a zone coverage. Or creeper blitzes, which are the same concept of rushing a typical coverage defender and having a typical pass rusher drop into coverage; it just doesn't present a blitz look pre-snap.

That was primarily how Leonard manufactured pressure in Week 1, and is a good way to keep a young or bad offensive line guessing. It makes it more difficult for the line to know where the pass-rush is coming from and can lead to missed communictions/assignments and free rushers for the defense. That's where not having a veteran center can really hurt because they have more experience to point out potential blitz or pass-rush threats pre-snap, versus a rookie who is just trying to not screw up the snap count.

A: If you had asked me this a week ago, I would have said no chance after watching how they struggled to stop the run during the preseason. However, I was very impressed by Leonard's scheme and have a lot more confidence that the defense can put up league-average numbers this year. There's definitely the potential to get up to being a Top 15 unit if they continue to play like they did last Sunday.

But to pour some cold water on the hot Raiders' defense, I don't want to overreact to a performance against a team competing for the No. 1 pick. So, this week — and really the next three games with the Chargers, Saints and Chiefs on the upcoming schedule — will be a better indicator for how good Las Vegas ' defense really is. If the unit continues to look strong down that stretch, now we're cooking with gasoline!

This Raiders team is well coached and well schemed and could be looking at .500 or better this year? Or the flip-side version: all they did was beat the Dolphins, and Miami is so bad it's going to make our players and scheme look great?

Kwity Paye/Treydan Stukes are going to be fringe Pro Bowlers?

A: The first bullet is the million-dollar question right now that we'll have a better answer to after Sunday. There's no doubt that the schedule makers threw Vegas a bone with the Week 1 matchup against Miami, and the Dolphins' roster is so young that it can give a false sense of hope for the Raiders moving forward. However, I was very impressed with Kubiak's and Leonard's play calling in Week 1.

Kubiak did an excellent job of finding creative ways to get Ashton Jeanty the ball, which was huge with Brock Bowers out and a cast of wide receivers that even the coach has admitted leaves something to be desired. Also, he did an excellent job with his 21 personnel packages , which again, is especially impressive without the team's best tight end.

Defensively, Leonard had all three levels constantly moving and, in addition to what was said above about manufacturing pressure, had a good scheme to get Maxx Crosby one-on-one matchups. My tone on the Tape Don't Lie film review conveyed this: I haven't been this excited about a defensive scheme from the Raiders in years.

A good scheme can translate from week to week and help overcome a talent gap. However, there are plenty of good coaches in the NFL, and it is still a talent-driven league. But I definitely think there is more reason to be optimistic about the Raiders moving forward, and that they can win more games than originally expected.

Paye and Stukes played pretty well last week, but calling them fringe Pro Bowlers would be a stretch at this point.

While he had eight pressures and two sacks in the opener, Paye is still a complementary rusher. He doesn't get a lot of quick wins, and his best trait is having a high motor. Those types of players are valuable to a defense because they can come up with clean-up sacks, where the coverage is holding up or another rusher wins but misses the tackle.

That's the difference between a quarterback extending the play and beating the defense on scrambles versus a drive-killing loss of yards. However, that's not exactly a Pro Bowl-caliber type of player since Paye's production is reliant on his teammates.

As for Stukes, he had the interception and a handful of impressive reps mixed in during his NFL debut. But he also had a few "rookie moments" with a missed assignment, a missed tackle and a play in coverage where he looked up for the ball late, resulting in a first-down catch.

Don't get me wrong, I was very encouraged with how the rookie played, especially considering it was his first start at a new position. However, let's pump the brakes a bit and let him play a few more games before we start throwing around the postseason accolades.

A: If the season opener was any indication, a lot!

Los Angeles gave up 393 yards to Arizona last week , which would have been the second-most its defense allowed all of last season. What's even more surprising is the Cardinals were viewed in the same category as the Dolphins heading into the season. Maybe that's a sign Arizona will be better than expected, but the Chargers also had a lot of missed assignments or moments where their defense wasn't on the same page.

That indicates the players aren't comfortable with the scheme yet, and that's surprising because the reason Harbaugh hired Chris O'Leary as defensive coordinator is that O'Leary was on the staff as the safeties coach under Minter in 2024. Presumably, that should mean the scheme is pretty similar to what the players are used to.

I can't say I've really dived into the differences between the Chargers' 2025 and 2026 defenses to know for sure. But you don't see a lot of former Western Michigan defensive coordinators making the jump to the NFL unless there's some familiarity with the club and the head coach wants to keep the scheme at least somewhat consistent.

To be fair, Week 1 can be screwy, as plenty of people have been reminding everyone that the Raiders beat the eventual AFC Champion Patriots last year. So, O'Leary can certainly turn things around after one bad game. However, the early returns aren't exactly high…

Q: With Kwity Paye, Malcolm Koonce and Patrick Johnson playing significant snaps, would Keyron Crawford have been inactive for the first month of the season anyway?

A: Maybe, but I'm also not 100% convinced that Johnson would have made the team if Crawford didn't get put on injured reserve ahead of cutdown day. The Raiders are only rostering four edges, and they weren't going to cut a rookie they just spent a Top 75 pick on. So, someone at another position who is currently on the roster would have been left off to keep Johnson as the fifth edge.

Granted, the coaching staff could have kept the veteran on the practice squad and called him up for the first three games to see if someone else got hurt to create an extra roster spot before having to promote him to the 53-man. Or they could have done some finagling where Johnson doesn't make the team initially, then a change or two happens after cutdown day, and he gets brought back that way, similar to what happened with Segun Olubi .

Ultimately, I think the decision to make Crawford or Johnson active on game day if they were both on the roster would have come down to who can contribute more on special teams.

According to Pro Football Focus , Johnson only played in six snaps defensively last week, but he logged 20 on special teams. Both players participated on special teams during the preseason, and for what it's worth, the veteran had the higher PFF grade in that department ( 72.5 to 61.4 ).

So, you could definitely be correct that Crawford wouldn't have been active even if he was healthy. I'm just not sure there would have been room for the 28-year-old had the rookie not suffered a significant injury.

Q: When exactly did Brock Bowers re-injure his knee, and when was the meniscus procedure performed?

A: To be clear, I don't have any sources or inside knowledge of this, so my answer is more speculative than factual.

I get the feeling that Bowers re-injured his knee either during or shortly after the first preseason game. The Raiders played the Cardinals on Aug. 13, where he played in just one snap (per PFF ) despite the rest of the starting offense getting a full 10-play drive. Four days later, videos on social media surfaced of him being ginger with the knee.

No first-stringers played in Houston , but Bowers did suit up against San Francisco and didn't quite look the same, according to my colleague Marcus Johnson . Marcus has a theory that the procedure actually happened shortly after the 49ers game, and that's unverified, but it would make more sense to me than Bowers going under the knife on the Tuesday before the season opener.

That timeline lines up better with the idea that he'll only have to miss "a game or two". Even if it was a minor surgery, I don't buy that someone can have their knee cut open and operated on and be ready to play in an NFL game 12 or 19 days later. On top of that, the situation doesn't make sense because it's the same knee Bowers injured last year, and it would be pretty dumb to rush a player who is a key part of the organization's long-term plan onto the field given the circumstances.

So, I don't have a hard answer for you. But the story, the way it's being presented, doesn't add up to me.

Q: I was wrong about DJ Glaze. I know the new coaching helped, but did Brady 's guy help him with his feet and lateral movement? Did he lose weight or get stronger?

A: I'm right there with ya! I thought Glaze was a prime candidate to get moved to guard, but he had an excellent game last week. What's even more impressive to me is that Chop Robinson has given Glaze problems in the past, going back to their college days, but the right tackle rose to the occasion.

Glaze is still listed at 331 pounds, so he doesn't appear to have dropped much weight. And, at least to me, he doesn't look much more slimmed down than he has in the past. But his footwork/footspeed did look improved in pass pro. Also, during training camp, Rick Dennison talked about getting Glaze to maximize his arm length, and Glaze's hand usage was much better than before.

In the past, he'd keep his hands very wide and invite pass-rushers into his chest rather than striking or punching to make the first significant contact. The third-year pro was much more consistent about keeping his hands tight to take advantage of his near 35-inch arms last Sunday. Hopefully, that continues moving forward.

Q: I thought Kirk Cousins was throwing pretty well at the end of last year with the Falcons. Are you surprised at his arm weakness? Did he injure his elbow again? Did this not show up in practices? I couldn't tell during his preseason outings.

A: I'm not surprised. In my opinion, Cousins' arm has been dead since he tore his Achilles during his last season in Minnesota (2023). That can impact a quarterback's ability to drive through the ground and use the legs to throw and get velocity on the ball, especially when the injury happens at 35 years old.

When the Raiders played the Falcons on Monday Night Football a couple of years ago, I noticed Cousins' arm was pretty weak when watching film leading up to the game. That popped up during the contest too, leading to him getting benched the following week.

Cousins did play better in relief of Michael Penix Jr . last year, but his arm is pretty dead at this point in his career. To me, there was a noticeable and significant difference between the velocity of his and Fernando Mendoza's passes during the preseason, and based on what beat reporters have said, that was the case during training camp, too.

To my knowledge, Cousins hasn't suffered another injury. He's just a 38-year-old trying to play a young man's game after a significant injury, and his arm is what it is at this stage: deceased.

A: Similar questions here from two different people, and I think my answer above shines enough light on my confidence in Captain Kirk, LOL! If you're struggling to read between the lines: it's not high!

Until Bowers is back in the fold (and completely healthy), the Raiders' offense is going to be highly dependent on the running game/Jeanty. Obviously, Las Vegas' rushing attack and, more specifically, the offensive line looked much improved last week. But this Sunday will test whether that was a fluke/more indicative of the opponent, or a sign that the unit is turning the corner.

For all that went wrong with the Chargers last week, they actually did a decent job of stopping the run. Yes, the Cardinals had 116 rushing yards as a team, but they only averaged 3.4 yards per carry , while running backs Tyler Allgeier and Jeremiyah Love were both under four yards a tote. Also, Los Angeles' 61.4 PFF run defense grade ranked 12th, and the club was 15th in Pro Football Network's run defense impact score (75.5).

It was the passing game that really did the Bolts' defense in, especially tight end Trey McBride , who was Arizona's leading receiver with nine catches for 95 yards and a touchdown. So, Bowers being doubtful for Sunday really hurts.

I have confidence that the Raiders' offensive line can continue to show growth. But, sorry for being repetitive, this week is the real test. I look at it like a college team playing an FCS School in Week 1 to build some confidence before turning around and playing an opponent of the same (or maybe even higher) caliber in Week 2.

Hopefully, Harbaugh doesn't take a page out of his alma mater's book and look like crap in the season opener, only to bounce back the following game. And yes, I'm considering Michigan 1-1 because that was some B.S. against Western Michigan! The Broncos won that game!

[Side note: this might be the first and last time WMU gets mentioned twice in the same article on this website!]

Q: Should we be surprised by how big of a contract that Michael Mayer got?

A: I was pretty shocked to see Mayer get a contract that made him the fourth-highest (now fifth-highest) paid tight end in the league. Honestly, I was shocked to see him get a contract extension ahead of the season in general.

I understand that Mayer can have a bigger role in Kubiak's offense, and the Raiders clearly believe in him long-term, so they're trying to get ahead of the market. But maybe wait, like, I don't know, four games to see how he performs in the new offense before handing out a big contract extension?

That's just my two cents, and I don't think anyone can reasonably say the body of work the 2024 second-round pick has done so far justifies top-five money at his position. Sure, he can get better and be more productive down the line, which is what the Raiders are betting on. But typically, players who get paid that much have both a strong track record and future value.

All of that being said, the devil is always in the details when it comes to contract extensions, and there was a lot of "sticker shock" when it comes to Mayer's new deal. Over the Cap dropped the structure of the contract earlier this week, and it's basically a one-year extension with two club options.

All of the guaranteed money is in 2027, and Vegas can cut him with a post-June 1 designation during the 2028 or 2029 offseasons while only taking on about $2.3 million of dead cap, per OTC, if things aren't going well. So, I have to give credit where credit is due and say that the organization and John Spytek did a good job protecting themselves while getting ahead of the market. That makes me more comfortable with Mayer's extension than the way it was initially reported.

That'll do it for this week's mailbag. Thank you all for submitting questions and, as your weekly reminder, if you'd like to have your questions answered in a future column, tweet them at me, @MHolder95 , email them to SBPQuestions1@gmail.com or look for our weekly call for questions on the site. The latter will continue to publish on Thursdays.

articles.body:
Brighton came into this match as the league's top scorers and did not disappoint with their attacking mindset.

But they worked hard in possession and when battling for the ball to deny Arsenal the space in which they thrive.

Diego Gomez on the wing did an excellent job of keeping Riccardo Calafiori quiet, while Charalampos Kostoulas caused problems for the Gunners backline throughout.

The 19-year-old Greece international deserved his excellent goal, which was his third in successive games, as he looks to show he can step up to be Brighton's main striker following Danny Welbeck 's summer departure to Chelsea .

But he was well supported by his team-mates, with Spaniard Chema Andres marking his first league start with a first goal for the club.

And then there was the 35-year-old Pascal Gross , who has rolled back the years with his performances so far.

The German, who rejoined the club in January from Borussia Dortmund , was again the conductor of Brighton's play and now has four goals in his last five games.

Fabian Hurzeler's side are packed with young talent and have a fearless approach that will cause problems and concern for any side - as both Manchester United and Arsenal found out over the past week.

articles.title: Player Ratings as Brighton Punish Arteta’s Side in 3-0 Loss
articles.summary: Arsenal Player Ratings vs Brighton: Havertz Struggles in Heavy 3-0 DefeatArsenal’s unbeaten start to the Premier League season ended in bruising fashion as B...
articles.body:
Arsenal Player Ratings vs Brighton : Havertz Struggles in Heavy 3-0 Defeat

Arsenal's unbeaten start to the Premier League season ended in bruising fashion as Brighton swept Mikel Arteta's side aside in a convincing 3-0 victory at the Amex Stadium.

There was an unsettling quality to Arsenal's performance from the opening exchanges. Brighton pressed with purpose, attacked loose possession and repeatedly found space as the visitors retreated towards their own penalty area.

Pascal Gross and Charalampos Kostoulas punished that passivity with strikes from distance before Chema Andres added Brighton's third from a corner after half-time.

For Arsenal, there were precious few positives. Declan Rice attempted to impose himself on midfield and Bukayo Saka provided occasional flashes of threat, yet Brighton consistently appeared quicker to loose balls and considerably more comfortable with the rhythm of the contest.

Arsenal Defence Endures Difficult Afternoon

Arsenal rarely established control from the back. Brighton's pressure caused problems in possession, while the reluctance to close down shooters proved particularly costly.

David Raya endured an uncertain opening and could have done better with Brighton's efforts from distance. Jurrien Timber looked understandably short of rhythm on his first start since March, while Ezri Konsa struggled when Brighton attacked directly.

Gabriel produced perhaps the most surprising performance. Usually so aggressive when stepping forward, the Brazilian repeatedly allowed Brighton space around the penalty area.

Arsenal were unable to deal with Brighton's intensity from the outset and Arteta found no convincing solution as the afternoon deteriorated. His substitutions offered limited improvement, leaving plenty to address after a 3-0 defeat that brought Arsenal's unbeaten opening to the campaign to an emphatic conclusion.

articles.title: Brighton 3 – Arsenal 0: write off
articles.summary: It’s been a while since Arsenal put in a “file and forget” performance but that is what they’ll need to do with today’s showing at Brighton. The Gunners, to...
articles.body:
It's been a while since Arsenal put in a "file and forget" performance but that is what they'll need to do with today's showing at Brighton. The Gunners, to a man, were well off their best. Brighton were energetic and more than a bit lucky. Combine those two and sometimes it can look like today's 3-0 loss.

There's a real risk of letting the scoreline over-influence the analysis of this match and to see bigger issues than are actually there. Arsenal had a bad day at the office. Brighton scored two goals from long-range shots. A match that on most days is 0-0 or 1-0 at halftime was 2-0. And that's that. Without two ridiculous goals against, Arsenal go in at half, adjust, and maybe things play out differently.

It looks and feels worse than it was because Brighton had so much energy and Arsenal made so many errors, many of them unforced. You could fairly say that the Seagulls' pressing unsettled the Gunners. But the pressing wasn't the reason for the scoreline. The point being that even granting Brighton were the better side, the thing that made them the better side wasn't the thing that made the outcome.

The first half goals were tremendously taken shots, both of which David Raya probably should have done better from — today will probably end up his worst showing of the season. The announcers criticized Arsenal for standing off both shooters but I don't think it was much of a mistake in either case. You typically let players shoot from out there because the shots are highly unlikely to find the back of the net. Unfortunately, Arsenal got the extremely short end of the stick in both instances.

In retrospect, Mikel Arteta looks to have gotten his lineup wrong. The Bruno Guimaraes-Declan Rice pairing isn't the one to go with against a team that presses as high and hard as Brighton. You really need one of Myles Lewis-Skelly or Martin Zubimendi on the pitch. Arteta's misstep was compounded by Bruno having an absolutely dreadful game. He misplaced several passes under very little pressure that short-circuited potential attacking moves and put the defense back under pressure. Bruno was also slow to react on an attacking move at 0-0 when he had a chance to do some damage after Riccardo Calafiori won a header.

Speaking of the Italian, he made a handful of similar mistakes to the Brazilian. On the break before Brighton's second goal, his pass took Martin Ødegaard much, much wider than he needed to go, which ultimately led to the move breaking down. The ball fell somewhat kindly for Bukayo Saka, but his tumbling effort went straight at Bart Verbruggen. At 3-0 down, Calafiori had time and space around the corner and blasted the ball across the box, far too hard for anybody to get on the end of.

That was just the kind of match it was. If it could go wrong, it did. Brighton scored a third from a corner kick where David Raya was blocked off from coming to claim the ball much in the way we were told they wanted to eliminate from the game. You're never going to get that call but at the same time, it's exactly what everybody was so up in arms about last season.

Down the other end of the pitch, an Arsenal corner just kind of sat in a dangerous area before getting knocked to safety. Bukayo Saka was in behind but his first touch / the bounce of the ball made it awkward enough that a defender had time to get across for a block.

It was just that kind of day. Not to put too fine a point on it, but today against Everton, Ipswich had a man shown a second yellow for diving. Ferdi Kadioglu threw himself to the ground in the Arsenal box, a clear dive that was emphatically waved off by the referee, but wasn't shown a second yellow. If it could go wrong (or at least not go Arsenal's way), it did. Better to get all that out of the system at once.

Arsenal lacked the sharp passing and the rotational support from off-ball players to effectively deal with the press. That's more on our guys (and perhaps the manager) than anything else. They didn't do the right things. When that's not working, the other option is to go long, but Kai Havertz really isn't the guy you want leading the line to do that. Viktor Gyokeres is much more willing to run behind and chase balls into the alleys. Arsenal's general lack of game-breaking pace across the front line hurt today more than usual, too. If you've got a guy that's going to win the footrace, you can simply tell that guy to run, boot it over the top, and profit. You can see the thinking behind Havertz over Gyokeres. Having another combination passer and technician to drop deeper can help pass through the press. But the poor passing limited that option.

When Arsenal did manage to pass through the press and threaten to break away, Brighton fouled from behind. The referee decline to book both Max de Cuyper and Diego Gomez early (and Martin Ødegaard later in the first half) for intentional fouls to stop the play after the press broke.

The one on Bruno Guimaraes in the center circle was particularly egregious. Arsenal had possessed the ball for a while. Brighton were in their shape. The Gunners were patient, recycled the ball, and finally coaxed the Seagulls to step up to press in the middle third. Bruno and Ødegaard worked a quick 1-2 in the middle to slip beyond it, and the Brazilian was hacked down from behind to prevent Arsenal attacking a defense that had been pulled out of shape and beaten. No booking.

It's a calculated risk that many clubs, Arsenal included, take. Brighton do it more than most. You usually come out ahead. That's why you do it. But if the referee decides he's not going to have intentional, tactical fouls from behind to stop the play and shows an early yellow card or two, you've got to find another way. Brighton did not have to find another way today.

It didn't make a difference in the match, but Viktor Gyokeres had a solid showing. He put Kai Havertz in on goal but the German volleyed straight at Bart Verbruggen. The Swede had another nice piece of play that Ebere Eze wasn't alert enough to capitalize on, too. As usual, Gyokeres had a couple instances of "he's refereed differently than most other strikers" too. He pinned his defender, tried to spin towards goal, and was slung to the ground — precisely the type of play that everyone fawns over Brian Brobbey about. It must be frustrating for Big Vik.

Four away matches in a row was always going to be tough. Arsenal caught Brighton at a particularly bad time, too. They're playing well and put in a solid performance today. That coincided with a decidedly off day from the Gunners. Oh well. Losing at Brighton isn't the end of the world. Glass half full — six of nine points from @Aston Villa, @Sunderland, and @Brighton is as good or better than pretty much everyone in the Premier League will manage this season. This match will leave a sour taste but you move on. I'd bet the lads will do so in short order, if they haven't already.

articles.title: Five Rutgers Players Who Can Establish Their Roles As Big Ten Play Begins
articles.summary: Who Has Stood Out During The First Couple Games For The Scarlet Knights?
articles.body:
After losing to UMass in the opener, the Scarlet Knights followed that up with a 28-21 loss to Boston College. Rutgers is now 0-2 heading into Big Ten play, with No. 12 USC coming to SHI Stadium on Saturday.

The preseason expectations are gone. There's really no point pretending otherwise.

But that doesn't mean the first two games have been completely useless from an evaluation standpoint.

Rutgers has gotten a chance to see several players in meaningful situations, and a handful of them have started to separate themselves. This isn't a list of the five best players on the roster. Guys like KJ Duff and Antwan Raymond have already established themselves as cornerstones for this team.

Instead, these are five players who could establish their roles as the season moves forward.

Moses Walker might be the easiest player to put on this list after what he did against Boston College.

Walker picked off two passes against the Boston College Eagles, recording the first two interceptions of his career. He also added a sack as Rutgers' defense forced three turnovers.

That's the kind of performance that can change how a player is viewed.

Rutgers needs playmakers on defense. The Scarlet Knights have had stretches where the defense looks capable of getting stops, but they have also struggled to consistently get off the field and have given up too many explosive plays.

Walker showed that he can create something when the opportunity is there. And after missing most of last season with injury, he was named as a Comeback Player of the Week due to his efforts to keep the Scarlet Knights in the game for as long as possible.

KJ Duff has already established himself as Rutgers' top receiving threat.

The next question is who can consistently give the Scarlet Knights something alongside him. Although Ben Black doubles Duff on the outside, Rutgers could use a reliable option in the slot.

Houston has been involved early in the season and has shown the ability to give Rutgers another option in the passing game. That's particularly important because Big Ten defenses are going to have a lot more ways to try to take Duff away.

As the starting slot wide receiver, Houston recorded four catches for 42 yards against UMass before adding five catches for 40 yards against Boston College. He can be a reliable option to pick up yardage on early passing downs, and with the quarterback situation as poor as it is, they could use all the short yardage they could get.

Clay Thevenin is another player whose role appears to be growing.

Thevenin had three carries against UMass, but his workload increased against Boston College. He carried the ball seven times for 36 yards and also recovered a fumble.

That's not exactly a massive statistical performance, but that's not really the point of this article. Thevenin is showing that he can contribute when his number is called.

Antwan Raymond has already established himself as one of Rutgers' most important offensive players, so this isn't about replacing him. Rutgers doesn't need Thevenin to suddenly become the starting running back.

During the second half at Chestnut Hill, the Knights had a physical one-two punch, and Thevenin mirrored Raymond's style by running uphill and fighting for extra yardage on the ground. Rutgers churned clock and pressured the Eagles' defense, unfortunately the offense was not able to capitalize enough to get the win.

That could prove to be useful, especially in Big Ten play, where running the ball is paramount to success.

Bradlee Jones hasn't necessarily produced the biggest numbers through two games, but he's another player who has shown the ability to make an impact play.

Jones forced a fumble against Boston College, giving Rutgers another example of a defensive player creating a turnover rather than simply making a routine tackle.

In a struggling secondary filled with newcomers, Jones posted a 91.8 PFF grade in run defense, 79.1 in tackling, and 46.5 in coverage, leading Rutgers' defensive backs with a defensive grade of 74.8. With speed being his biggest attribute, the Citadel transfer should be starting at left cornerback while Kevyn Humes is a strong candidate to start opposite him, especially with Kevin Levy and Mikey Munn getting injured early last week.

Rutgers picked up defensive end Sekou Kromah in the transfer portal late in the summer after he was ruled eligible by a court ruling. At 6' 3" and 275 pounds, Kromah has the size to immediately anchor the defensive line and put pressure on opposing quarterbacks.

The Temple transfer had two tackles in his Rutgers debut against UMass, but against BC, he had three tackles including one for loss. More importantly, he recorded three pressures against the Eagles, showing his potential to be disruptive to opposing quarterbacks.

Last season, Kromah tallied 14 tackles with 4.5 for loss and three sacks, including a sack at #18 Georgia Tech. In Temple's home game against #13 Oklahoma, he was a force to be reckoned with, posting seven tackles, 2.5 TFLs, a sack, and a pass breakup. Look for that talent to travel to Piscataway this season.

Farell Gnago deserves a mention here as well.

Gnago may not be getting the same number of snaps as some of the other players on this list, but he's one of those players who seems to make an impact whenever he's on the field.

That's something I've noticed dating back to last season, when Gnago helped force a fumble that led to Rutgers' game-winning field goal at Purdue.

It doesn't always have to be a huge statistical performance. Gnago just seems to find a way to make a play — whether it's getting into the backfield, making a stop or creating some kind of disruption.

He could spend a lot of this season playing second-team snaps, but that doesn't mean he can't carve out a role. He currently has Rutgers' lone sack of the season, which he registered against UMass.

Gnago has shown that he can make his snaps count. He has earned a bigger role with the defense.

There's no changing the fact that Rutgers is 0-2.

The losses to UMass and Boston College are on the record, and now the Scarlet Knights have to move forward with one of the toughest games on their schedule.

USC is coming to Piscataway, and Rutgers will have a chance to see how some of these early-season developments translate against one of the better teams on its schedule.

But even with the season already going off course, Rutgers still has an opportunity to figure out what it has.

Walker has shown he can make game-impacting plays on defense. Houston can potentially become another important receiver to complement Duff. Thevenin is earning more opportunities in the backfield. Jones has shown a knack for creating turnovers. Kromah has been disruptive up front. And Gnago remains a player worth watching whenever he gets onto the field.

There are ten games left. Rutgers has the responsibility to find out what they have on this roster.

articles.title: Athlete of the Week: Sauquoit Valley’s Colton Larsen
articles.summary: Webster’s Dictionary defines the word “versatile” as “embracing a variety of subjects, fields, or skills,” and Sauquoit Valley junior QB Colton Larsen embrac...
articles.body:
Webster's Dictionary defines the word "versatile" as "embracing a variety of subjects, fields, or skills," and Sauquoit Valley junior QB Colton Larsen embraces that word fully.

"Keeps me in shape as a player, especially because I play three sports," Larsen said. "Having adversity around the field helps me push myself to become a better athlete. Definitely gotta keep a clear head. If something goes wrong on offense or kicking, just gotta have a clear head, put it in the past and focus on the future."

"He's been a weapon in all phases of the game for us, we knew that coming into the season, having watched his film, realizing his athletic ability, he's one of those kids that can kind of do anything," Sauquoit Valley football head coach Jason Alexander said. "He also leads by example, and he's a great leader on the field. Above and beyond just the physical characteristics, it's the leadership characteristics as well."

Larsen plays in all three phases for the Red Hawks, playing QB, DB, and kicking the football, including the game-winner as time expired against Little Falls.

"It's definitely something I'll remember for the rest of my life," Larsen said.

"I'm thrilled for them as a team, I'm thrilled for him as an individual as well," Alexander said. "It took a lot of mental toughness in that moment for us collectively and for him to keep his focus and go out there and do what he does."

As Sauquoit Valley has transitioned from playing 8-man back to 11-man football, Larsen's leadership and maturity have been a major help.

"He's matured as a football player and as a young man," Alexander said. "He was a very young quarterback last year, a sophomore, and he's a junior this year, and he's developed that sense of maturity just keeping his focus and setting the tone for the rest of the kids and trying to be more vocal about it as now a junior this year. He's trying to speak out and lead in that way as well. He's done a great job with it. He really has."

articles.title: Everton 1-0 Ipswich: What O'Neil said
articles.summary: Ipswich remain without a clean sheet in each of their last 24 Premier League games, extending their worst run without one in the top-flight.  Ipswich Town's...
articles.body:
Ipswich Town manager Gary O'Neil speaking to BBC Sport: "I thought we were unfortunate to leave with nothing, we gave a lot and looked a threat. We conceded a very unfortunate goal. The main criticism of the performance is that we didn't show the cutting edge that we have in recent weeks."

On Abdul Fatawu 's sending off: "I've seen them given, I've seen them not given. It looks like he is anticipating contact - and there is contact. I can understand it being a yellow card. Where it is on the pitch, I don't think the referee needs to get involved. I've spoken to him, he has been excellent for us. I suppose the lack of experience... it's making sure when you're on a yellow card that you don't take any risks. I thought we were excellent with 10-men and the home fans were restless.

"The only disappointment is the result. Liverpool and Manchester United are Champions League clubs where you just have a go, but against Sunderland , Crystal Palace and Everton we have shown we can be very competitive.

"We will get ready again for Fulham . Disappointed we have such a break [for the international break], they're a great group to work with."

Ipswich remain without a clean sheet in each of their last 24 Premier League games, extending their worst run without one in the top-flight.

Ipswich Town's Gary O'Neil has lost 50 of his 93 Premier League games as a manager, the seventh quickest to that tally. David Moyes has inflicted more of those defeats on him than any other coach (five).

articles.title: At least one team has called Steelers about Joey Porter Jr.
articles.summary: Friday's deep dive from ESPN into the far-simpler-than-it-seems contract issue between the Steelers and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. included a contention that...
articles.body:
Friday's deep dive from ESPN into the far-simpler-than-it-seems contract issue between the Steelers and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. included a contention that the team has not received any " serious inquiries " regarding a trade. As one source put it in response, the Steelers could be trying to prevent a trade market from materializing.

We're told that at least one team has called the Steelers about Porter. Whether that qualifies as a "serious inquiry" is a matter of interpretation.

The Steelers apparently want to keep Porter, for now. If they start actively negotiating a trade, the situation could take on a life of its own and quickly become an inevitability. (A fait accompli , if you're feeling fancy.)

The issue for now, as we understand it, is that the Steelers want a lot. We're told it's in the neighborhood of a first-round pick or a second-round pick, plus a third-round pick.

And here's where the dog starts chasing its tail. If the Steelers will apply that kind of value to Porter in a trade, why won't they offer him a contract that he'll take?

The threshold impediment continues to be the outdated internal rule that no new deals will be done after the regular season starts. That doesn't matter unless and until the two sides are close. They still aren't.

The trade deadline arrives in 52 days. This looks like it will keep unfolding one week at a time, until the Steelers decide to pay Porter or to allow the inquiry (or inquiries) to become "serious."

It can happen quickly. Last year, the Cowboys abruptly decided to trade linebacker Micah Parsons after realizing that he fully intended to not play in 2025, due to a back issue, until he got the contract he wanted. Through two weeks, Porter is implementing that same approach.

The options are few. Pay him, trade him, play hardball in the hopes of getting him to blink, or do nothing — and pay him a weekly game check to not play.

The best play in the end may be to throw the door open to any and all interested teams, and to take the best offer they get.

articles.title: Dana White calls ex-WWE star's injury 'worst in Power Slap or UFC history'
articles.summary: Former WWE champion Jake Hager required emergency surgery after being slapped by Johnny Magna during a Power Slap event in Las Vegas.
articles.body:
Former WWE champion Jake Hager, known in the ring as Jack Swagger, suffered a severe injury that required emergency surgery after he was slapped by Johnny Magna during a Power Slap event in Las Vegas.

The incident occurred in the second round, when Magna delivered a powerful slap that landed across Hager's face. It is believed that one of Magna's fingers inadvertently struck Hager's left eye, prompting Hager to immediately clutch his face and inform the referee that he had been hit in the eye.

Moments later, blood began to stream from Hager's eye, resulting in the ringside doctor halting the match on the spot. Hager was rushed for emergency eye surgery to address the injury.

Dana White called the injury the "worst injury in Power Slap or UFC history," and so gruesome that he refused to let the production team air a replay.

See Dana White's career as UFC president, from breaking up fights to RNC speeches

Power Slap , a slap-fighting competition created in 2022 and co-owned by UFC president Dana White, pits two competitors against each other, each delivering open-hand strikes under strict rules. The results of the matches are decided by knockout or judges' decision.

Hager, who wrestled as Jack Swagger from 2006 to 2017, joined Power Slap in March. He won his debut by knockout in April, then suffered back-to-back stoppage losses.

articles.title: Steelers get trade update on Joey Porter Jr.
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers received a trade update on Joey Porter Jr. as the relationship between both sides appears to have hit an all-time low.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have been bombarded by Joey Porter Jr. drama and trade rumors over the past several weeks, but an insider update has shed light on the league's potential interest in the young cornerback.

According to ESPN's Brooke Pryor and Jeremy Fowler, the Steelers haven't received or sent out "any serious inquiries" regarding a Porter trade, despite the significant number of rumors that have come out recently.

"The Steelers could trade Porter, though the team has neither made nor received any serious inquiries about the cornerback," Fowler and Pryor wrote. "One NFL executive believes the Steelers could get a second-round pick in exchange for Porter and a quality Day 3 draft selection."

Not allowing a touchdown in coverage when targeted since 2023, Porter has quickly emerged as one of the NFL's top cornerbacks. But trade partners aren't exactly throwing themselves at the Steelers to acquire Porter. A lack of interceptions, zero personal accolades like Pro Bowl and All-Pro honors, Pittsburgh's high asking price, and the fact that Porter is seeking a huge extension have likely played a role in deterring trade suitors.

This actually works out best for the Steelers, as Porter's impact goes beyond interceptions and Pro Bowl nominations. The lack of a trade market could force Porter to play out his rookie deal with Pittsburgh, which should lead to the team franchise tagging him after this season in order to restart contract negotiations.

articles.title: Broncos get nightmare Week 2 ESPN prediction that could put season in jeopardy
articles.summary: This prediction could have the 2026 Broncos season at risk after two weeks.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos were blown out by the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. It was a brutal loss that raised uncomfortable questions just one week into the season.

While Sean Payton and the Broncos should be able to rebound going forward, it won't be easy in Week 2 against the Jacksonville Jaguars . They've been red-hot for a while now and could pose a threat to the Broncos in Denver.

ESPN's Pamela Maldonado predicts that this Week 2 matchup will have a nightmare-ish result for the Broncos. Maldonado predicts Denver will lose their Week 2 matchup, drop to 0-2 on the year, and put their 2026 season at risk already.

Broncos predicted to drop to 0-2 by ESPN analyst

"Denver's offense hasn't shown enough to justify laying points. The Broncos produced only 176 yards and 3.6 yards per play in their Week 1 loss to the Chiefs," Maldonado writes. "... Defense makes the Broncos the favorite, but the Jaguars have the more trustworthy offense to win outright."

While the Broncos might be favored in this game, as it's a home matchup, and that Week 1 performance might be a fluke, the Jaguars have been playing great football for a while now.

They demolished the Cleveland Browns in Week 1. It wasn't just the Jaguars offense that thrived; their defense was shut down for most of the game, allowing a long garbage-time touchdown to give Cleveland their only TD of the day in Week 1.

Considering how poorly the Broncos offense performed in Week 1 against the Chiefs, it wouldn't be that much of a stretch to believe this Jaguars defense will stay hot and shut down the Broncos offense in Week 2.

If this prediction were to come true, and the Jaguars do upset the Broncos and send the Broncos to a 0-2 record after Week 2, there will be some real doubts creeping in about this team.

Whether it's about Bo Nix , the defense, Jaylen Waddle , Davis Webb , or Payton and the entire front office, an 0-2 start to the season after a near Super Bowl trip would be quite the rough start to the year.

Their season wouldn't be over, but such a poor start would give the Broncos little margin for error the rest of the season. With a difficult schedule the rest of the way, a 0-2 start to the season, as Maldonado predicts, could put the Broncos' season at risk already.

articles.title: Here's what we learned in Arizona high school football, Sept. 17-18
articles.summary: There were bounce backs, big plays, wild finishes, and revenge, as Arizona HS football teams made statements in games played Sept. 17-18, 2026.
articles.body:
There were bounce backs, wild finishes, big plays, more blowouts and revenge, as Arizona high school football teams made statements in games played on Sept. 17-18.

The Arizona Republic rewinds the week and looks ahead as the season drama takes big turns.

What we learned. Basha isn't going anywhere

There is no quit in Chandler Basha , which entered the season No. 1, drawing plenty of accolades before losing two straight games for the first time since 2020. Eight starters were injured, contributing to that skid. But the Bears (2-2) showed up in an impressive 30-22 win over No. 2-ranked Peoria Liberty (3-1) on Sept. 18, proving their season is far from over. If the Bears get healthy, this team is going to be tough to stop.

The defense turned up the heat with a big hit from Barry Adams, which popped the ball loose from quarterback Jason Haines and led to Taylan Patterson scooping it up and running 38 yards for a third-quarter touchdown that gave the Bears a 24-14 lead. The game turned in Basha's favor, as Haines and company had no answers until the final few minutes. By then, it was too late.

It was a master class coaching job by Chris McDonald to get these guys up for what had become their biggest game of the year. The banged-up secondary featured two freshmen and a sophomore. And quarterback Jake Rogers, who had a 22-yard scoring run, was playing most of the final three quarters with a banged-up shoulder.

It was no surprise that Scottsdale Saguaro lost to Glendale Mountain Ridge and former top Saguaro assistant coach Andrew Johnson on Friday, Sept. 18. But Saguaro returning to the field since losing to Scottsdale Desert Mountain in the Aug. 28 opener was big enough for the Sabercats, which had to cancel two games due to injuries on an already depleted roster. This once-dominant program is rising back from the ashes and the small step it took, albeit a 45-6 loss, was significant. Coach Butch Goncharoff made clear after the game the team will play this out and learn some valuable life lessons along the way.

ALA Gilbert North coach Ty Detmer has done a tremendous job since taking over the Eagles' program two years ago. He doesn't have many star players like Goodyear Desert Edge, but his No. 4 Eagles (Republic's 5A rankings) pulled off maybe the stunner of the week with a 33-30 win over the host and No. 1 Scorpions on Friday, Sept. 18.

The Eagles drove down the field, before Ben Livingston hit Cam Shepard for a 5-yard score with about six minutes to play that was the difference. The defense came through with a fourth-and-short stop and the Eagles ran out the clock with a couple of first downs. "Our boys played with great effort all night," Detmer said. "Didn't flinch when things went wrong, and answered every time we got down. Proud of their effort and resilience."

The 5A Conference is showing some parity with No. 2 Scottsdale Desert Mountain and Goodyear Millennium both in the mix, along with Desert Edge, ALA Gilbert North and Horizon in the chase for the gold ball in December. Desert Mountain (4-0), which has outscored its opponents 223-14 with three shutouts, faces Horizon (4-0) on Oct. 23. Desert Edge and Millennium meet on Oct. 30.

This might have to go to Phoenix Maryvale with its 30-24 win over a good Mesa Eastmark team. Miles Woods had three touchdowns, two on offense and one on defense. Eastmark was ranked No. 3 in 4A by MaxPreps/AIA. Maryvale was ranked 22nd. This win came a week after Gilbert Mesquite rallied to beat Maryvale 30-28, the only loss by the 3-1 Panthers. The Carter twins — Marcus and Mark — have done a great job in their two years as co-head coaches. Their home game Sept. 25 against San Tan Valley Combs (3-1) will be another chance for the Panthers to show they're deserving of a 4A state playoff spot.

Phoenix Brophy Prep built a 28-12 lead in the first half, only to see Mesa Mountain View take control of the second half and score on two long, time-consuming drives and convert two-point plays to tie it at 28 with about four minutes to play. But the Broncos wouldn't let down in the end, as Ryder Noche returned a kickoff to midfield, before the Broncos drove down to set up a last-second, 18-yard field goal by Jack Carson. "Give Mountain View a ton of credit," Brophy coach Jason Jewell said. "They held the ball in the second half and went on two long drives that ate up most of the entire second half." This sets up a huge game for the Broncos (3-1) against 3-1 Chandler on Thursday, Sept. 24, at Phoenix Central.

Eagar Round Valley exacted revenge in a 56-0 rout of Lakeside Blue Ridge in a 3A football game. Last year, Round Valley's only loss on its way to the 3A gold ball came against Blue Ridge. This was the season debut of star running back Brody Crick, who had one touch, which ended up going for a 22-yard scoring pass play. Round Valley improved to 5-0 with a big game Sept. 24 at 4-1 Payson, which was stunned by Joe Germaine's ALA Mesa North team, 26-14, on Sept. 18.

Horizon super soph Dylan Brush ran for more than 407 yards and six touchdowns in a 55-36 5A win over Phoenix Sunnyslope. Brush has 17 rushing TDs in the Huskies' 4-0 start.

Chandler Lincoln Prep rolled to a 54-0 rout of Tucson Catalina, as sophomore running back Josh Morris ran eight times for 134 yards and a touchdown. He also had two pancake blocks that sprung two punt returns for touchdowns.

Peoria Centennial (4-0) relied on its gritty defense for the second week in a row to beat a good Mesa team, 20-7, as defensive end/linebacker Luke Franklin had nine tackles and two sacks and Michael Ware and JoJo Gonzalez both had interceptions. Torrin Hill caught seven passes for more than 100 yards and a touchdown.

Phoenix Arcadia sophomore quarterback Carter Lampe had the biggest game of his young career with 319 yards and four touchdowns passing in a 45-9 win over Glendale Deer Valley. He completed 10 of 12 passes.

Gilbert Higley turned in its best defensive effort in a 36-0 6A win over Gilbert Highland, as Dax White had nine tackles and Nasim Eason intercepted a pass. Quarterback Anthony Palka ran for 104 yards and passed for 177 yards and two TDs.

Glendale Ironwood coach Tony Stilling had high praise for his offensive line after a 29-20 win over Glendale Raymond S Kellis. The line paved the way for 389 rushing yards on 46 carries, as 10 players ran the ball, including two — Ramsey Pyne and Edison Unger — who had more than 100 yards. The line was anchored by right guard Jaxson Jauregui. "Our line as a whole was the main reason that we racked up 389 rushing yards," Stillings said.

Phoenix Sandra Day O'Connor, under second-year coach Ben Kullos, is on the rise after successive wins over Mesa Red Mountain (45-35) and Tucson Salpointe Catholic (36-7). The Eagles are 3-1, with the only loss coming on a walk-off 47-yard field goal in a 31-28 setback to Mesa.

Three-time defending 1A champion Winkelman Hayden extended its winning streak to 41 games with a 57-6 rout of Superior. It's the state's longest active winning streak.

articles.title: Millwall goalkeeper alleges he was spat at by West Ham’s Taty Castellanos
articles.summary: Goalkeeper Filip Marschall alleged that he was spat at by the forward Taty during an altercation between the players in the second half
articles.body:
Millwall goalkeeper Filip Marschall alleged that West Ham forward Taty Castellanos spat at him during the meeting of the London rivals at The Den on Saturday.

The incident came in the 65th minute of the derby and as goalkeeper Marschall delayed releasing the ball from his hands while his side were leading 2-0.

The West Ham forward Taty looked to close Marschall down before he picked up the ball, before the players appeared to get involved in an altercation in the penalty area.

Marschall then appeared to point towards his jersey, gesturing that he was spat at. TV footage of the incident was inconclusive.

Lions boss Alex Neil confirmed the allegation afterwards, saying: "I believe so. Fil was saying to the referee throughout the game when that happened, at that point.

"Obviously I'm so far away so it's hard for me to see what happened, but I wouldn't presume Fil would say that without cause, if you like, so I don't know. I'm sure the referees and the authorities, whoever, will look at it and if it warrants that it needs dealt with, I'm sure they will."

Castellanos could face a six-match ban if the Argentine is found to have spat at Marschall.

Hammers boss Nuno Espirito Santo said: "I didn't see, so I'm not going to comment on any allegations. I didn't see it. And that's not what we should be speaking about [in] this game, this game has much to speak about, it was a very intense game for both fans."

Millwall and West Ham were meeting for the first time in 14 years, following the Hammers' relegation to the Championship, with a large-scale Metropolitan Police operation planned in east London.

Millwall dominated the first half at The Den and led the Championship leaders 2-0 when the flashpoint occurred.

Marschall had the ball in his hands when he was closed down by West Ham forward Taty. Confusingly, referee Paul Tierney then appeared to signal a corner after Marschall went over the eight seconds permitted to restart play.

West Ham quickly took the corner, with Taty crossing for fellow half-time substitute Pablo to finish into the empty net, but referee Tierney halted the play and summoned both captains to the penalty box and instead signalled for Marschall to restart play.

Argentine forward Taty then closed down Marschall for a second time, with the goalkeeper delaying the restart before picking the ball up, which is when the alleged spitting incident reportedly took place.

Sky Sports reported that Marschall delayed releasing the ball because he claimed that Taty had spat at him, with the Millwall coaching staff reporting the allegations to the fourth official on the touchline.

The incident was also something of a turning point in a pulsating east London derby, with West Ham recovering from an awful start to salvage a 2-2 draw at The Den.

West Ham's Mohamadou Kante pulled one back from 25 yards in the 74th minute before Konstantinos Mavropanos grabbed the equaliser in the 80th minute when he headed in a cross.

Kante was then sent off for pulling down Millwall's Kyrell Lisbie when he was the last man and Lisbie was through on goal, but the 10 men of West Ham held on to claim a point.

Meanwhile, a total of six arrests were made after 400 police officers threw a "ring of steel" at The Den on Saturday, to ensure there was no repeat of the violence which has marred this fixture in previous seasons.

The force said the match took place "without significant disruption" across south east London, adding a total of six arrests were made as of 4pm on Saturday.

articles.title: FSU football's depth chart for Week 3 vs. Alabama
articles.summary: The FSU Seminoles have revelaed their depth chart for their Week 3 game against the Alabama Crimson Tide. See the changes here.
articles.body:
The Florida State Seminoles have released their depth chart ahead of their Week 3 game against the Alabama Crimson Tide on Monday, with Kolby Crawford of Noles247 sharing the lineup on social media.

The depth chart features several changes from the one they announced in Week 1 ahead of their game against the SMU Mustangs . Freshman wide receiver EJ White has replaced Tae'Shaun Gelsey as the backup to Jayvan Boggs . Gelsey missed the first two games of the season and is reportedly questionable to play.

There have also been some changes along the offensive line. Nate Pabst and Chimdia Nwaiwu are now listed as co-starters at right tackle, with Paul Bowling and Pabst now co-starters at right guard. Nwaiwu started the first two games but struggled, with Pabst taking over against SMU and Bowling sliding into right guard when Pabst moved over. Sean Poret is no longer listed after backing up Pabst at right guard.

The defense also features several changes, with them now only listing two linebacker spots after listing three in the first two games. The now-deleted spot was shared by Caleb LaValee and Blake Nichelson .

LaValee has replaced Izayia Williams, who will miss the rest of the season with an injury, as Chris Jones ' backup, and Nichelson is no longer listed and is expected to miss some time with an injury. Max Redmon has been added as the backup to Ashlynd Barker at rover, replacing Donny Heibert, who is no longer listed.

The game between FSU and Alabama is set to start at 3:30 p.m. ET in Bryant-Denny Stadium. The game will be on ABC. Here is a look at FSU's entire starting lineup against Alabama.
